Because of your little faith. REFLECTIONS TODAY Earlier, Jesus had summoned his Twelve disciples and given them authority over unclean spirits to drive them out and cure every disease and every illness (Mt 10:1). When the missionaries returned, they, like the 72 disciples, must have reported with joy that even demons were subject to them in Jesus’ name (see Lk 10:17). Yet, in this episode the Twelve who have attempted to heal the boy who has a demon are unsuccessful. Jesus rebukes the demon, and the demon comes out of the boy. When the disciples privately ask Jesus why they could not cast out the demon, he tells them it was because of their little faith (Greek oligopistis). In the imagery used by Jesus, faith the size of the smallest garden seed (mustard) is enough to move mountains. Hence “little faith” is powerless because it is practically nothing. It is merely an intellectual assent to something presented; it lacks deep conviction. Peter illustrates what little faith is: he ventures into danger by sharing Jesus’ power to walk on the water, but he loses his focus, yields to his fears, and sinks (Mt 14:28-30). In the same manner, the disciples who failed as exorcists have ventured to face the dangerous demoniac-lunatic presuming that they shared Jesus’ power to exorcise. But they may have lost their focus, gotten distracted by the epileptic seizures, the incredible feats of their opponent, and yielded to their fears. Or they may have used Jesus’ name as a magical tool or instrument, expecting instant results at its mere mechanical utterance. Our faith should be placed not in magic, not in our own abilities, but in God’s boundless power and mercy. We should trust in the power of Jesus to heal and transform lives. Gospel • Matthew 17:14-20 A man came up to Jesus, knelt down before him, and said, “Lord, have pity on my son, for he is a lunatic and suffers severely; often he falls into fire, and often into water. I brought him to your disciples, but they could not cure him.” Jesus said in reply, “O faithless and perverse generation, how long will I be with you? How long will I endure you? Bring him here to me.” Jesus rebuked him and the demon came out of him, and from that hour the boy was cured. Then the disciples approached Jesus in private and said, “Why could we not drive it out?” He said to them, “Because of your little faith. Amen, I say to you, if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you.” Source: “365 Days with the Lord 2026,” St. Paul’s, 7708 St. Paul Rd., SAV, Makati City (Phils.); Tel.: 632-895-9701; E-mail: publishing@stpauls.ph; Website: http://www.stpauls.ph.

PH as ‘Eala Village’, every court an ‘Eala Center’. HOTSPOT Millions have stayed up many times to watch Alex Eala play tennis abroad. We are like in vigils deep into Philippine nights, supportive of Eala and eager to witness her notch victories that usher in extra beautiful mornings in the country. The only thing missing in Eala’s wins is the raising of the tricolor to the tune of Lupang Hinirang. But the void is more than filled up by Filipinos themselves waving the flag and cheering and shouting from the stands in the courts where Eala plays. We love Eala to bits because she’s excellent in tennis and the prospects that she can attain greater glory for herself and to the people she professes to love. She’s also thoughtful and articulate, seems immune from the perils of celebrity. She’s a proud Filipina whose sense of patriotism is matched only by Filipinos’ most avid, raucous and unmitigated fandom. For a people fed up living in seemingly-perpetual dark times, staying up late to watch Eala gives people a reason to hope that a new morning is coming. When she won her first WTA championship in the Mubadala DC Open, Eala became “the first-ever and hopefully the first of many.” As of press time, Eala has won her debut at the Canadian Open in Toronto, by beating American Alycia Parks. Apologies for the puns but I can't help it. It seems the Philippines is now one big “Eala Village” and every court where she plays an “Eala Center.” If the trend continues, it would be good news to Philippine tennis fandom and also to the promotion of tennis and enticing young Filipinos to take the racket as well. In a few years, the University of the Philippines would almost certainly invite Eala to teach, perhaps alongside Yulo. It would be a terrible mistake if sports development programs would not invite them to lend their experience and to reach our people about their sports and the paths they took towards global glory. We have seen this before, when Hidilyn Diaz won the country’s first Olympic gold in Tokyo, and when Carlos Yulo won two Olympic golds in Paris. And even before when other Filipino athletes fought and won in world and Asian championships. They always give Filipinos a fresh sense of pride, and also give to the world our capacity for global greatness. The Department of Education and the Commission on Higher Education should redesign certain public schools and state colleges and universities to include facilities for weightlifting, artistic gymnastics, tennis, and other sports apart from basketball. Other sports where Filipinos could compete and excel are volleyball and football. If the government can quickly and without question allot 1,620 hectares for an America-led technology project, then there's no acceptable excuse not to provide space for sports facilities in all regions of the country. I hope to see citizen Manny Pacquiao lead Filipino athletes in pressing both the House and the Senate, as well as Malacanang, to do what's right for Filipino athletes and Philippine sports. (Hopefully, the future sports infrastructure would be corruption-free!) In the case of Eala and Yulo, they affirm and confirm that young Filipinos remain our bearers of flag and hope. All they have achieved are monumental and historic, and consequential to the country. May they inspire others, and may their efforts reenergize the “once young” to support sports and youth development, and to not give in to hopelessness and cynicism. For now, we follow Eala’s upward climb to tennis greatness. We don't mind the vigils late into the night. We don't mind if she suffers defeats, as all athletes do along the way. What we mind is seeing a Filipina valiantly compete and aspire to win in the highest levels of world tennis. With Filipinos abroad going in droves to cheer for her in competitions, we here at home join them virtually in an exercise of hope and for that awesome feeling of national achievement. I don't mind if we get used to seeing one or many of us compete at the highest levels of tennis and other sports. That could only be positive for a nation looking for new visions, new heroes and new directions. For this and for her being her amazing self, we must thank and continue to support Alex Eala and the other young athletes whose efforts bring out the best in us for all the world to see.

Angelica Lopez of Palawan wins first Reina Filipinas crown. Angelica Lopez of Palawan, Alexie Brooks of Iloilo, and Anne Patricia Lorenzo Diaz of Manila emerged top winners at the inaugural Reina Filipinas beauty pageant held at the Newport Performing Arts Theater on Friday, Aug. 7. Lopez was crowned Reina Filipinas Grand International 2027. Meanwhile, Brooks and Diaz were both crowned Reina Filipinas MGI All Stars . Completing the roster of winners in the first Reina Filipinas pageant were Cleopatra Barrera of Zambales, who was named first runner-up; Isabella Ortega of Camarines Sur, who finished as second runner-up; Zeah Nestle Pala of Mandaluyong, who placed third runner-up; and Luisa Lorin Benavides of Caloocan, who was named fourth runner-up. During the final question-and-answer portion, the seven finalists were asked: “There are undeniably so many pageants already. What space do you hope Reina Filipinas would occupy?” Lopez answered: “I understand that every pageant serves a purpose, and so does Reina Filipinas. Here, they have a business that gives women the opportunity to learn new skills, become more empowered, and grow as individuals—whether in sports, entertainment, or business. It is truly a meaningful and empowering platform, creating a win-win situation for everyone so that we can all move forward toward progress, development, and productivity.”

How one of Philippines’ richest families prevents heir syndrome. You will not find the third generation of Gokongweis in the boardroom—they are testing food formulas in research laboratories, managing animal feed mills in Cebu, and supervising operations on factory floors. For the four cousins currently working inside JG Summit Holdings Inc. and its affiliate companies, that ground-level experience is intentional. As the conglomerate prepares for an eventual generational transition, the family is doing away with executive fast tracks. Out of 50 third-generation cousins, only four currently work for the business, and none hold corporate board seats or executive titles. The most visible heir so far is Justin Gokongwei Pe, son of Robina Gokongwei-Pe, who works on the manufacturing side at consumer food maker Universal Robina Corp. (URC). Two other cousins are based in Cebu, overseeing animal feed operations and shopping mall leasing. A fourth cousin, a trained chemical engineer, works in product research and development for the food division. Keeping the enterprise grounded comes down to giving younger family members room to choose their own career paths, according to Lance Gokongwei, president and chief executive officer of JG Summit. “It’s our job in the second generation to, I guess, make it attractive for them to join the business in the future, because they have so many choices available to them,” Gokongwei said. “You know, kids of the next generation have so many choices and their own aspirations—many of them want to prove themselves outside in their own independent capacity,” he added. That management philosophy extends to his own household. Lance’s children, aged 23 and 20, are building work experience outside the conglomerate, with a focus on technology. “If they’re interested and qualified, then hopefully I will try to attract them to join the business,” Gokongwei said. “They’re definitely much more tech-savvy than I am, and right now, they’re gaining experience outside the business.” The decision to enforce operational training comes during a challenging operating environment for multi-industry groups. Higher global oil prices have increased fuel costs for budget airline unit Cebu Air Inc., pushing the parent firm to rely on its balance sheet strength and consumer food sales to help absorb market volatility. Whether more members of the 50-cousin cohort choose to join the business will depend on whether this bottom-up framework proves successful over time. “Fundamentally, we hope they carry the same values that Mr. John and his brothers had: integrity, hard work, prudence, and an entrepreneurial spirit,” Gokongwei said, referring to his late father, founder John Gokongwei Jr. “Beyond that, it’s about having the continued boldness to dream, finding solutions for customers, and pursuing new opportunities,” he concluded.

Palace warns public against being used for money as ‘Maleta Boys’ case unravels. Malacañang has urged Filipinos not to allow themselves to be used in exchange for money to fabricate allegations, warning that innocent people could be harmed as the controversy involving the so-called “Maleta Boys” continued to unfold. In a video statement on Friday evening, Aug. 7, Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro said the public should not be lured by financial offers to participate in what she described as a scheme to make up stories against the President. "Kaya sa mga kababayan natin ay huwag magpabitag sa ganitong plano para lang sa pera dahil may mga taong inosente ang inyong sisirain (So, to our fellow Filipinos, do not fall into this kind of scheme just for money because there are innocent people whose lives you will destroy),” she said. Castro specifically linked the alleged scheme to supporters of former president Rodrigo Duterte who are supposedly out to destroy the reputation of President Marcos. "Nakikita naman natin ang style ng mga Duterte supporters kung paano sila mag-hire ng mga tao na gumawa ng kathang-isip na kwento kapalit ng malaking halaga, laban sa Pangulo (We can see the style of the Duterte supporters in how they hire people to make up fabricated stories against the President in exchange for a large amount of money),” she said. The Palace Press Officer added that the controversy was also being viewed by some as part of an alleged effort to destabilize the Marcos administration, citing former Quezon City congressman Mike Defensor and his associates. "Marami nakakaramdam na parte ito ng plano ni Mike Defensor at ibang kasamahan niya para sa isang destabilisasyon (Many feel that this is part of the plan of Mike Defensor and some of his associates for a destabilization effort),” she said. Despite this, Castro said any findings from the Office of the Ombudsman concerning the "Maleta Boys" allegations against former House Speaker Martin Romualdez and other personalities should be left to the independent constitutional body. Castro's remarks came as four of the so-called "Maleta Boys" recanted their earlier statements implicating Romualdez, Marcos, and other personalities in the alleged flood control scandal. One of the group members, however, claimed that they were offered between P20 million and P25 million to recant their statements, adding another layer to the controversy. Meanwhile, 10 members of the group were arrested after they failed to post bail in connection with perjury charges filed against them.

US request for Quiboloy extradition needs thorough evaluation —Palace. Malacañang said that the US government's request to extradite Kingdom of Jesus Christ founder Pastor Apollo Quiboloy must undergo careful evaluation and assessment before the Philippine government decides how to proceed. In a video statement, Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro said the request should be resolved at the proper time to ensure the highest level of justice for the alleged victims in the Philippines and the United States, as well as for Quiboloy, who is facing charges. Quiboloy faces US charges involving alleged sex trafficking, visa fraud, and bulk cash smuggling, among others, while he also faces criminal proceedings in the Philippines. “Ang paghiling ng US government para sa extradition ni Pastor Quiboloy… ay isang bagay na dapat na pag-isipan, ma-evaluate, ma-assess at ma-resolba sa tamang panahon para makamtan ang pinakamataas na antas ng hustisya (The US government's request for the extradition of Pastor Quiboloy to stand trial there in the US… is something that must be considered, evaluated, assessed, and resolved at the proper time to achieve the highest level of justice),” she said Friday evening, Aug. 7. Castro stressed that the government's consideration of the request should take into account not only those who allegedly suffered from the offenses but also the rights of the accused. “Hustisya para sa mga ‘di umanong biktima rito at sa US, at pati na rin sa akusado (Justice for the alleged victims here and in the US, as well as for the accused),” she said. DOJ to review records According to Castro, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) had received the US extradition request and endorsed it to the Department of Justice (DOJ), which received the voluminous records on Friday. “Ayon sa DOJ, sa Lunes nila ito sisimulang pag-aralan (According to the DOJ, they will begin studying it on Monday),” she said. Philippine Ambassador to the United States Jose Manuel “Babe” Romualdez said US authorities were eager for the Philippines to resolve the extradition request, with the matter now in the hands of Philippine authorities. If extradition is eventually approved, Romualdez said US Marshals would likely take custody of Quiboloy and bring him to the US jurisdiction where the alleged offenses were committed. Quiboloy's arrest Quiboloy was taken into government custody on Sept. 8, 2024, after he surrendered to authorities inside the 30-hectare KOJC compound in Davao City following a 16-day police operation to serve his arrest warrant. The operation began on Aug. 24, 2024, when more than 2,000 police officers were deployed to the compound as authorities sought to locate Quiboloy and serve the warrant. The Philippine National Police later said Quiboloy surrendered after authorities gave him a 24-hour ultimatum to come out of the building where he was believed to be hiding, with negotiations involving the PNP and the Armed Forces of the Philippines leading to his surrender. Quiboloy and four co-accused were flown from Davao City to Manila that evening and brought to the PNP custodial facility at Camp Crame in Quezon City. The arrest followed Philippine court warrants in connection with qualified human trafficking and child abuse cases, while Quiboloy was also facing federal charges in the United States. Quiboloy has denied the allegations against him and pleaded not guilty to the Philippine qualified human trafficking charges. US cases, Philippine proceedings The US government has accused the detained televangelist of sex trafficking and other offenses, including allegations involving the recruitment and exploitation of women and children. The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) previously placed Quiboloy on its most-wanted list in connection with allegations of sex trafficking, conspiracy, and bulk cash smuggling, among other offenses. The Philippine cases, meanwhile, have continued separately, with Quiboloy remaining detained while proceedings are ongoing. A Pasig court in 2025 rejected his request for hospital arrest, ruling that there was no compelling reason to transfer him from detention to a hospital facility. Quiboloy ran for senator in the May 2025 elections while detained, but failed to win a seat, finishing 31st in the senatorial race. Marcos, Quiboloy ties Quiboloy endorsed Marcos' presidential bid and then Davao City Mayor Sara Duterte's vice presidential bid in the 2022 elections, publicly declaring his support for the Marcos-Duterte UniTeam during a campaign event at the KOJC compound in Davao City. Quiboloy was also a close ally of the Duterte family and served as spiritual adviser to former president Rodrigo Duterte, giving him significant political visibility before and during the 2022 campaign. The political connection has since drawn attention as Quiboloy faced criminal proceedings in the Philippines and the United States, although the Palace has maintained that the cases should be handled through the proper legal process.

Barbers: Zero sincerity from VP Duterte to account for P612.5-M confidential funds. In over four years, Vice President Sara Duterte showed no sincerity to properly liquidate the P612.5 million in confidential funds that were released to offices under her control--specifically the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and Department of Education (DepEd). Thus, said House impeachment adviser Robert Ace Barbers, even as witnesses from the Commission on Audit (COA) testified on the agencies' liquidation deficiencies in Duterte’s ongoing Senate impeachment trial. “Since 2022, it seems that wala pa ring sincere effort to liquidate. Kasi 2026 na ngayon,” Barbers said during a virtual press conference Friday, Aug. 7. (Since 2022, it seems there has still been no sincere effort to liquidate. Because it is already 2026.) “Until now, sa aking paniwala, no single piece of liquidation na sinubmit nila, eh acceptable per the joint circular,” he noted. (Until now, in my view, no single piece of liquidation they submitted is acceptable under the joint circular.) Barbers, also a House prosecution panel spokesperson, was referring to Joint Circular (JC) No. 2015-01, which governed the usage of confidential and intelligence funds. The confidential funds under scrutiny in the trial-- particularly under article I of the articles of impeachment --total P612.5 million, consisting of P500 million released to the OVP from the fourth quarter of 2022 to the third quarter of 2023 and P112.5 million released to the DepEd. Respondent Duterte served as education secretary from 2022 to 2024. Prosecution witness COA auditor Roderick Wamil had told senator-judges that the OVP and DepEd repeatedly failed to comply with the JC as far as the P612.5 million was concerned. Wamil identified unsupported reward payments, non-allowable expenditures, the absence of documentary proof of payments and other deficiencies that prompted the issuance of audit observation memoranda (AOMs). The state auditor also testified that the liquidation reports and certifications bore Duterte’s signature as head of both agencies. Barbers said the repeated audit findings showed that the liquidation documents submitted over the years still failed to satisfy government auditing requirements. “Kaya nga nagkaroon ng red flags, kaya nga nagkaroon ng audit observation memoranda, kaya nagkaroon ng notices of disallowance, kasi lahat ng na-submit for the last four years ay hindi acceptable and in accordance with the [JC],” he said. (That is why there are red flags, audit observation memoranda, and notices of disallowance, because everything submitted over the last four years is not acceptable and not in accordance with the JC.) Why acknowledgment receipts? Barbers also questioned why acknowledgment receipts (ARs) bearing the name of suspected fictitious recipient "Mary Grace Piattos", "Andy Lim", "Kokoy Villamin" and many others remained the principal liquidation documents four years later. “Kung meron talagang recipient ’yung confidential and intelligence funds na ’yan, ang tanong lang lagi na namumuo sa isipan ng ating mga kababayan ay bakit ARs?” he said. (If those confidential and intelligence funds truly have recipients, the question that always arises in the minds of our people is why only ARs?) According to Wamil, the OVP under Duterte was the first government agency in nearly 10 years to submit only ARs to liquidate confidential funds . The witness, who served from September 2014 to February 2024 with the ICFAO, said he had audited the confidential funds of more than 30 national government agencies, as well as numerous local government units (LGUs). Barbers has also pointed to what he described as discrepancies in the dates appearing on some ARs, saying some appeared to have been prepared a year after the confidential funds had been released. He noted that the COA had already issued two AOMs, but said no compliance had been submitted even after the second memorandum. Barbers added that even if recipients used assumed names or aliases for security reasons, the joint circular still required accomplishment reports to be submitted. “Kung merong mga tao na gumamit ng ibang pangalan pero nakatanggap ng pondo, eh meron pong kaakibat na report ’yan na dapat isinasubmit in a sealed envelope. Doon natin makikita kung naging successful ba ’yung intelligence and surveillance gathering nila kasi gumamit tayo ng pondo ng bayan eh,” he explained. (If there are people who used another name but received funds, then there is a corresponding report that must be submitted in a sealed envelope. That’s where we will see if their intelligence and surveillance gathering was successful, because we used public funds.) Barbers maintained that the issue was about accountability for public funds, not politics or the 2028 elections. “This has nothing to do with politics, nor not even 2028. Because 2022 pa ito, hanggang ngayon ay hindi pa rin nasasagot. Gusto lamang malaman ng taong-bayan kung anong katotohanan sa likod ng usapin tungkol sa confidential funds,” he said. (This has nothing to do with politics, nor even 2028. Because this dates back to 2022, and until now it remains unanswered. The people simply want to know the truth behind the issue of confidential funds.) Duterte had earlier declared her intention to run for president in 2028.

Graduates seek timelines on Mayor Isko’s housing, jobs, healthcare vow. Graduating students on Friday welcomed Manila Mayor Francisco “Isko Moreno" Domagoso’s pledge to continue investing in housing, education, healthcare, and jobs, but called for clear timelines and concrete results as they prepare to enter the workforce. Speaking after the 59th Commencement Exercises of the Eulogio Amang Rodriguez Institute of Science and Technology at the Philippine International Convention Center , several members of the Class of 2026 said the mayor’s message addressed their concerns—but needs follow-through. “Maganda pong marinig na may plano, pero sana may malinaw na timeline kung kailan mararamdaman (It’s good to hear there’s a plan, but we hope there’s a clear timeline on when people will actually feel it),” one graduate said, citing job opportunities as a top concern. Domagoso, in his speech, assured graduates that the city would stay focused on what he described as “Minimum Basic Needs,” including housing, education, healthcare, and employment. “Sabay-sabay tayong lalaban tungo sa maayos na kinabukasan (We will all strive together toward a better future),” he said, addressing graduates and their families. He also pledged to manage city resources responsibly, saying he would strive daily to serve as an effective steward of public funds. But for some students, the challenge lies beyond commitments. “Hindi lang dapat pangako. Sana mas mapabilis ang trabaho at mas maging accessible ang healthcare at housing (It shouldn’t just be a promise. Work should be sped up, and healthcare and housing should be made more accessible),” another graduate said. Others pointed to the need for stronger support systems as fresh graduates transition into the job market, including skills matching and employment placement. Domagoso said the city government would “move in parallel” with graduates as they build their futures, but attendees said coordination between programs and actual opportunities will be key. “As graduates, ready na kami (we are ready),” one student said. “Sana ready rin ang lungsod para tulungan kami (Hopefully, the city is also ready to support us).” The ceremony gathered hundreds of graduates and their families, marking a milestone for students now facing a more uncertain job landscape while looking to local government for support.

Hungarian envoy receives Order of Sikatuna. President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. conferred the Order of Sikatuna on outgoing Hungarian Ambassador to the Philippines Dr. Titanilla Tóth, recognizing her contributions to strengthening relations between the Philippines and Hungary as she concludes her diplomatic posting in Manila. Tóth received the honor during her farewell call on the President at Malacañan Palace on July 29. “It’s always a little bit sad to see you go. But thank you for everything that you have done,” Marcos told the ambassador, adding that she would have many reasons to return to the Philippines. The Order of Sikatuna is among the highest distinctions conferred by the Philippine government on foreign diplomats and officials who have contributed significantly to the country’s international relations. Established in 1953, the order takes its name from Datu Sikatuna of Bohol and the historic blood compact with Spanish explorer Miguel López de Legazpi in 1565. Tóth leaves Manila after a posting that saw Philippine-Hungarian cooperation expand across diplomacy, trade, education, agriculture, research, and cultural exchange. The Philippines and Hungary established diplomatic relations in 1973. In recent years, Hungary has also supported the early conclusion of negotiations for a Philippines-European Union Free Trade Agreement, which is expected to further expand opportunities for trade and investment. As part of her farewell engagements, Tóth met with Senate President Sherwin “Win” Gatchalian, with discussions touching on interparliamentary dialogue, educational cooperation, and people-to-people ties between the two countries. She also paid a farewell call on Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro, where both sides looked back on developments in bilateral relations during her tenure. The Department of Foreign Affairs recognized the Hungarian Embassy’s work in promoting cultural diplomacy and educational exchanges, as well as cooperation in agriculture, research, trade, and other areas of mutual interest. Education has been an important component of Hungary’s engagement with the Philippines, complementing broader efforts to create stronger links between institutions and people in both countries. Tóth’s final round of meetings reflected the range of relationships cultivated during her posting—from the country’s highest political offices to institutions involved in education, culture, research, and commerce. Her departure closes one chapter in a diplomatic relationship now spanning more than five decades, with both Manila and Budapest looking to build on the areas of cooperation developed during her tenure.

Mysterious caskets draw reactions from advocacy groups. Advocacy groups on Friday, August 7, said the mysterious caskets found in several parts of Metro Manila reflect mounting public frustration over tensions in the West Philippine Sea (WPS), even as authorities continue to investigate who left the items and the motive behind them. The groups, Alyansa ng Bantay sa Kapayapaan at Demokrasya (ABKD), People’s Alliance for Democracy and Reforms (PADER), Liga Independencia Pilipinas (LIPI), and the Filipinos Do Not Yield Movement (FDNY), said the caskets appeared to symbolize sentiments that many Filipinos have long wanted to express amid ongoing maritime disputes. “The caskets may be anonymous, but the message is not, Filipinos have had enough,” said Dr. Jose Antonio Goitia, chairman emeritus of the four organizations, noting that the display reflects growing dissatisfaction over reported harassment of Filipino fishermen, obstruction of Philippine Coast Guard and Navy missions, and challenges to the country’s sovereign rights. The groups echoed the sentiment, while clarifying that their criticism is directed at policies and actions they believe violate Philippine sovereignty and international law, not at ordinary Chinese citizens. They also urged the government to continue asserting the country’s rights through diplomatic channels. Authorities earlier recovered the caskets from parts of Manila, Quezon City, Caloocan, and Makati. Police said the items contained crumpled papers and bore anti-CPP-NPA and anti-China messages. The Quezon City Police District (QCPD) said it has identified the driver and vehicle allegedly used to unload one of the caskets, providing a key lead in the investigation. Police have yet to determine those responsible or whether the display was intended as a protest or another form of expression.

Fraternity at the heart of PH-France ties. For outgoing French Ambassador Marie Fontanel, there was one word that best described her three years in the Philippines: “fraternité”. It was fitting, then, that fraternity—the third of the French Republic’s ideals of “Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité”—became the theme of Fontanel’s final Bastille Day reception as ambassador, held on July 14 at the Fairmont Makati. “Fraternity is not just a word on the walls of our institutions,” Fontanel told guests. “It is the common house we build together every day.” The idea carried particular meaning for an ambassador preparing to say goodbye. Fontanel spoke warmly of the welcome extended to her and her family—her husband Alan and their children Luis, Tuan, and Gabriel—and described their years in Manila as “an incredible journey of friendship.” That friendship was also reflected in a bilateral relationship that saw significant developments during her posting. Among the most consequential was the signing earlier this year of a Status of Visiting Forces Agreement between France and the Philippines, making France the first European country to enter into such an arrangement with Manila. Cooperation also expanded in maritime security, energy, agriculture, infrastructure, transportation and environmental protection, alongside growing economic and development ties. But diplomacy during Fontanel’s tenure was hardly confined to government meeting rooms. French culture remained a familiar presence in the Philippines through initiatives such as the French Film Festival, Fête de la Musique and Goût de France, while scholarships, alumni programs and the Partnership for Youth in the Philippines created more opportunities for exchanges between Filipinos and the French. Fontanel also used her farewell reception to turn attention away from France itself and toward the Filipino communities and organizations she had encountered during her posting. Performances by the Virlanie Foundation choir and NGO Cameleon placed civil society at the center of the evening, reflecting the ambassador’s broader interpretation of fraternity as something practiced rather than simply proclaimed. She paid tribute to organizations working with vulnerable communities, particularly women and children, as well as those involved in education, culture and social inclusion. For Fontanel, these relationships offered perhaps the clearest expression of what diplomacy ultimately seeks to accomplish. “All those initiatives pursue the same objective—bringing people together and building a future based on trust and cooperation, a true definition of fraternity,” she said. It was an unusually personal note on which to mark a national day, but an appropriate one for an ambassador at the end of her assignment. Bilateral relations are often measured through agreements signed, trade figures and official visits. Fontanel’s farewell offered another measure: the relationships built in between. And after three years in Manila, fraternité was the French word she chose to leave behind.

The story behind Alex Eala’s sampaguita earrings at the National Bank Open. While watching Alex Eala’s match against Alycia Parks live on television, I could not stop looking at the pink earrings she wore on Centre Court. They stood out each time the camera moved closer. The match took place on Aug. 5, 2026, during the second round of the National Bank Open presented by Rogers, a Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) 1000 tournament held at Sobeys Stadium in Toronto, Canada. Alex defeated Alycia, 6-1, 4-6, 6-2, to advance to the third round. After the match, we came across a tribute to Alex on the Kristine Dee Jewellery Instagram account: “What it’s like to be Filipino. Watching you compete with grace, courage, and heart fills us with so much pride. You have become a meaningful symbol of hope for our nation, showing the world what Filipino excellence, resilience, and humility look like. Your wisdom shines not only on the court, but in your words as well. You bring families, friends, and an entire country together, reminding us that there is so much to believe in. Congratulations on this incredible milestone. We’re all cheering you on, Alex!” We immediately reached out to Kristine, who confirmed that she had made them especially for Alex and personally gave her the pair in Manila before the tennis player left for her tournaments in the United States and Canada. The designer had no idea if and when Alex would wear her gift, so seeing them during an international match came as a lovely surprise. “It was truly an honor that she wore them,” she tells Manila Bulletin Lifestyle. Inspired by the national flower Set in 14-karat gold, the design combines small white pearls and diamonds with a sampaguita hand-carved from pink mother-of-pearl. Kristine chose the section of shell with the richest, most even tone for the center flower. “I felt that particular pink would enhance her beauty and make her glow more, and it did,” she says. “The sampaguita’s petals are intentional. Eight pieces for luck,” shares Kristine. She added small white pearls for freshness and “bango,” the Filipino word for a pleasant fragrance, and to symbolize grace. The choice of flower was equally personal. Kristine used the sampaguita to represent Eala’s courage, passion, grace, and Filipino pride. “Just for Alex,” she says of the one-and-only original design. She can create a similar pair upon request, but it will be made “with a twist.” A gift made out of admiration Kristine describes herself as a big fan of Eala. Giving the earrings directly to the tennis player was already meaningful, but she did not expect Eala to wear them during an international match. She became emotional watching the nation’s pride play before a packed stadium, with Filipino supporters cheering her on. “Naiyak ako (I was moved to tears) when I saw it,” she says. “Ang ganda-ganda lalo ni Alex (Alex looked even more beautiful).” For Kristine, the earrings were made entirely out of love.

Mayor Isko urges graduates to brace for life beyond school. Manila Mayor Francisco "Isko Moreno" Domagoso on Friday, August 7 urged graduates of Eulogio "Amang" Rodriguez Institute of Science and Technology to prepare for the realities of life beyond school, warning that challenges and failures await after they leave the classroom. Speaking at the school’s 59th Commencement Exercises at the Philippine International Convention Center , Domagoso told the Class of 2026 that earning a diploma is only the beginning of a more difficult journey. “Sa tunay na kalagayan ng lipunan, marami pa kayong pagsubok na dadaanan. Dadaan pa kayo sa maraming pagsubok and failure (In the real state of society, you will go through many trials. You will face many tests and failures),” he said. The Manila mayor stressed that setbacks are inevitable and should not be feared, noting that failure can help build resilience and deepen understanding. “Failure sometimes makes you strong emotionally and gives you more understanding and experience,” he said. Domagoso also reminded the graduates that their future will depend largely on their own decisions, saying no one else can define their path. “Nobody will write your story, not your parents, not your friends, not your teachers, deans, and me. It is only up to you,” he said. Drawing from his own experience, Domagoso recounted growing up in poverty and taking on various jobs before entering public service, underscoring that life does not always follow one’s original plans. “Anong pangarap ko? Maging kapitan ng barko. Anong binigay sa akin ng Diyos? Maging kapitan ng lungsod ng Maynila (What was my dream? To become a ship captain. What did God give me? To become the captain of the city of Manila),” he said. He added that the next chapter of the graduates’ lives remains unwritten. “Walang laman ang mga pahina ng libro ng buhay ninyo; kayo ang gagawa niyan (The pages of your life’s book are blank; you will write them),” he said.

LTFRB suspends operation of taxi in viral overcharging of foreign tourist. The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) warned taxi drivers of overcharging commuters following the case of a cabbie who demanded P2000 from a foreign tourist for a five-minute trip from the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA). On Saturday, Aug. 8, LTFRB chairman Vigor D. Mendoza II said they already suspended for 30 days the operation of the involved taxi and asked the operator to explain why the franchise should not be revoked over the incident. He also encouraged the public to report abuses to the LTFRB and in the case of this incident, he said this was monitored by the agency’s social media team after the victim posted a video of the incident. Based on the vlog, the taxi driver charged a foreigner P2,000 for a short trip from the airport to the destination and the worst part is that the driver also allowed another person to ride on the vehicle. “This is a gross violation of the franchise rules and regulations. No passenger, much more foreign tourists whom we should welcome to the country, deserves this kind of treatment,” said Mendoza. “But we will give the operator the chance to explain as part of the due process. In the meantime, however, the operation of that taxi is temporarily suspended,” he added. The operator was also tasked to surrender the license plate of the taxi on or before the Aug. 19 hearing. The operator was also directed to have the taxi driver involved to undergo both a road safety seminar and a drug test. Mendoza said these were all stated in the show cause order issued to the operator which also asked for an explanation why no sanction should be imposed for glaring violation of for the alleged failure to provide safe, reliable, and convenient public land transportation service. This is aside from the case of overcharging of fare.

PNP tells public: 911 can also be used for disaster-related emergencies. The Philippine National Police (PNP) urged the public to maximize the use of the Unified 911 hotline during disasters and calamities to ensure faster emergency response and improve public safety. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr. said the Unified 911 Hotline connects callers to the police, fire, medical, and rescue services through a single emergency number. “This hotline was not created solely to address crimes but also to respond to the needs of all our kababayan during natural calamities, including typhoons,” Nartatez said. “Whether for preemptive evacuation, search and rescue operations, or other emergencies, this hotline is a lifeline for everybody,” he added. Nartatez said early reporting of emergencies allows responders to act faster, especially during severe weather when every minute can save lives, adding that the PNP wants more Filipinos to become aware of the hotline and use it whenever immediate assistance is needed. He said the hotline is an important part of the government's disaster preparedness efforts and complements the response of local government units and other emergency responders. Nartatez said the they continue to strengthen their emergency response capability through the Unified 911 hotline as part of the efforts to provide faster and more accessible public service during emergencies

Driver in Manila casket drop arrested. A 51-year-old driver was arrested in Bulacan within hours after one of the abandoned caskets was discovered in Sta. Cruz, Manila, marking the first concrete development in the investigation into the unusual display that surfaced across Metro Manila. The suspect, Perigrino Miculob, was apprehended at around 6 p.m. on Aug. 7 inside Marilao Grand Villas in Loma de Gato, Marilao, Bulacan, following backtracking operations. Authorities said the operation led to the identification of the vehicle allegedly used, a Toyota Hi-Ace van (plate number NKQ 9818), which was recovered as part of the probe. Investigators are working to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incident and determine possible accomplices. The Manila Police District (MPD) told Manila Bulletin Miculob was allegedly the one who left the casket found in Sta. Cruz, adding that more details will be released as the investigation progresses. Police have yet to determine the full motive behind the act but noted that the coordinated appearance of the caskets suggests planning and execution involving multiple locations. Caskets were earlier recovered in at least five areas across Metro Manila, including Sta. Cruz in Manila; Welcome Rotonda and Boy Scout Circle in Quezon City; as well as sites in Caloocan and Makati. Initial examination showed the caskets contained crumpled paper and carried banners with anti-CPP-NPA and anti-China messages. Authorities said case build-up is ongoing and appropriate charges are being prepared against the suspect, while parallel efforts continue to identify other individuals who may have taken part in the coordinated drops.

Timog double-slay suspect nabbed in Lanao drug bust. A 38-year-old man linked to the April 28 fatal shooting of businessman “Perry” and his driver in Quezon City was arrested during a drug buy-bust operation in Kapatagan, Lanao del Norte, on Aug. 6. Alias “Kidong,” a resident of Barangay Poblacion, Kapatagan, was nabbed at around 1:45 p.m. in Purok 10, Poblacion, during the operation conducted by the Kapatagan Municipal Police Station (MPS) and other police units. Police recovered 1.30 grams of shabu worth P8,840 from him. The operation was carried out by the Kapatagan MPS in coordination with the 1005th Regional Mobile Force Battalion-10 (RMFB-10), Provincial Intelligence Unit (PIU), Provincial Drug Enforcement Unit (PDEU) of Lanao del Norte, and 2nd Provincial Mobile Force Company (PMFC). The shooting that killed “Perry” and his driver happened in the area of Timog Avenue and EDSA in Quezon City on April 28. On July 13, the Quezon City Police District (QCPD) filed two counts of murder against the individuals involved in the case. Kidong also has previous cases for alleged violations of Republic Act No. 11235, or the Motorcycle Crime Prevention Act, and Republic Act No. 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002. He remains in the custody of the Kapatagan MPS for the filing of appropriate charges for violation of RA 9165. The QCPD is coordinating with police units in Lanao del Norte for the necessary legal procedures in connection with the double murder case.

Lapu-Lapu welcomes Olympians, 48 nations for IRONMAN 70.3. LAPU-LAPU CITY – Olympic pedigree, a stacked international field and one of Asia’s toughest race courses promise another thrilling spectacle when the IRONMAN 70.3 Lapu-Lapu blasts off Sunday, Aug. 9, at Mactan Newtown Beach in Cebu, where defending champion Henri Schoeman returns determined to reclaim the crown against a deep cast of elite challengers. The South African star, who captured the bronze medal in the Rio Olympics, is back after missing last year's race and eager to build on the commanding victory he posted in his event debut in 2024. But the 34-year-old faces a far sterner challenge this time, with fellow Olympian Natalie Van Coevorden leading a stellar women's field and an equally determined international cast targeting the professional titles. The centerpiece of Sunrise Events, Inc.'s premier endurance race presented by Megaworld will once again test athletes over the grueling 1.9-km swim, 90-km bike and 21-km run, highlighted by the iconic Cebu-Cordova Link Expressway (CCLEX). Its sweeping sea views, relentless crosswinds and rolling terrain have become defining features of the bike leg, while Cebu's tropical heat and humidity ensure that strength alone will not be enough to conquer the course. More than 1,400 athletes from 48 countries are entered in the landmark 12th staging of the race, underscoring its sustained growth into one of the most respected stops on the global IRONMAN circuit. Over the past decade, the event has consistently attracted world-class pros and thousands of age-group competitors while earning praise for its organization and race execution. Competing nations include Australia, Austria, Barbados, Belgium, Canada, China, Colombia, Czech Republic, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Guam, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Kenya, Korea, Macao, Malaysia, Morocco, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Papua New Guinea, Qatar, Reunion, Russia, Serbia, Singapore, South Africa, Spain, Sri Lanka, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates, Uganda, the United Kingdom, the United States and Vietnam. Schoeman, however, will have little room for error against a formidable men's field featuring Austria's Sebastian Fuchs, New Zealand's Brett Clifford, Christian Davey and Ben Hamilton, China's Miao Hao, Singapore's Aaron Kiss, Australia's John Fothergill and American Thomas Iñigo, among other international standouts eager to make their mark. Their presence sets up another high-caliber duel of endurance, speed and race strategy on a course widely regarded as one of the most demanding on the Asian circuit, where weather, terrain and tactical execution often prove as decisive as physical fitness. The women's pro race is expected to be just as compelling with Australia's Van Coevorden taking center stage. Ranked No. 1 in Oceania and No. 24 in the World Triathlon Series, the 33-year-old Campbelltown native returns to familiar ground after winning the women's elite title in the 2011 Subic Bay ITU Triathlon Asian Cup. But Van Coevorden will also have to contend with a quality field that includes Sarah Thomas, Cassandra Heaslip, Paige Cranage, Charlotte McShane and Emily Donker, all capable of producing podium-worthy performances in the marquee endurance event. Local interest, meanwhile, will focus on the Filipino Elite Category, led by Jewin Ochea and Raymund Torio. Established by the Philippine Sports Commission, the division serves as a vital pathway for the country's top triathletes, bridging the gap between age-group racing and the international professional ranks while showcasing homegrown talent. Beyond the elite competition, the event offers age-group athletes an opportunity that extends well beyond race day. As an official qualifier for the 2027 IRONMAN 70.3 World Championship, the Cebu leg gives Filipino competitors a rare chance to secure world championship berths on home soil. A total of 50 qualifying slots will be available, including 25 reserved for women as part of IRONMAN's continuing commitment to promoting gender equality and expanding female participation in the sport. Successful qualifiers will advance to the 2027 IRONMAN 70.3 World Championship on Aug. 28-29, 2027 in Chattanooga, Tennessee. Spicing up the event is the Sunrise Sprint, a beginner-friendly race featuring a 750-m swim, 25km bike and 5km run, giving first-time multisport athletes an opportunity to experience racing on one of Asia's premier triathlon stages. Equally defining the event is the extraordinary community support that has become a hallmark of IRONMAN Lapu-Lapu. Thousands of schoolchildren and local residents are once again expected to line the race route, transforming the competition into one of the most vibrant and memorable stops on the international triathlon calendar. More than a showcase of world-class endurance racing, IRONMAN 70.3 Lapu-Lapu has evolved into a celebration of sportsmanship, volunteerism and community pride, with residents embracing athletes from around the globe while inspiring the next generation through the values of perseverance, discipline and excellence. With Olympians, seasoned pros, emerging local stars and thousands of determined age-group competitors converging on a championship-caliber course, the IRONMAN 70.3 Lapu-Lapu is once again primed to deliver a memorable test of endurance – and another unforgettable chapter in one of Asia's premier triathlon destinations. From the first swimmers entering the water to the final finishers crossing the line, enthusiastic spectators provide an emotional lift for every competitor—from professionals chasing podium finishes to first-time participants pursuing personal milestones. Their energy has long distinguished the Cebu race from other events on the circuit. --//
