Typhoon Dolphin enhances 'habagat,' brings heavy rains over parts of PH—PAGASA. Typhoon Dolphin is enhancing the southwest monsoon or “habagat,” which is bringing heavy rains particularly over the western section of Luzon and rainy conditions over other parts of the country, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said on Saturday, Aug. 8. PAGASA weather specialist Veronica Torres said Dolphin remains unlikely to enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) or directly affect any part of the country. “Ito namang bagyong [Dolphin] ito ay mababa ‘yung tiyansang pumasok ng ating Philippine Area of Responsibility at magkaroon ng direktang epekto sa kahit anong parte ng ating bansa (This typhoon, Dolphin, has a low chance of entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility and directly affecting any part of the country),” she said. “Gayunpaman, nahahatak nga nito ‘yung southwest monsoon o habagat na nakakaapekto sa may Luzon at Visayas (However, it is enhancing the southwest monsoon or habagat, which is affecting Luzon and the Visayas),” she added. According to Torres, the enhancement of the habagat is causing heavy rains, especially over western Luzon, while much of Luzon, the Visayas, and parts of Mindanao are experiencing rainy conditions. “At dahil nga nahahatak nito ‘yung habagat, nagkakaroon nga tayo ng mga malalakas na pag-ulan lalo na sa western section ng Luzon at nagiging maulan nga ‘yung malaking bahagi ng Luzon, Visayas, and some parts of Mindanao (And because it is enhancing the habagat, we are experiencing heavy rains, especially over the western section of Luzon, while a large portion of Luzon, the Visayas, and some parts of Mindanao are experiencing rainy conditions),” she said. As of 3 a.m., PAGASA said Dolphin was located 810 kilometers northeast of extreme Northern Luzon. It noted that the typhoon was packing maximum sustained winds of 155 kilometers per hour (kph) and gustiness of up to 190 kph while moving southwest at 15 kph. Meanwhile, the state weather bureau said it is also monitoring a low-pressure area (LPA) outside PAR that has a high chance of developing into a tropical cyclone within the next 24 hours. “Ganoon pa man, mababa naman ‘yung tiyansang magkaroon ito ng direktang epekto sa ating bansa, at mababa rin ‘yung tiyansang pumasok ng ating Philippine Area of Responsibility (Nevertheless, it has a low chance of directly affecting our country, and it also has a low chance of entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility),” she added. Torres advised the public to continue monitoring PAGASA updates.

‘Enjoy Your Stay’: Difficult, uncomfortable, enlightening. Let us put it out there pronto: “Enjoy Your Stay” is a difficult watch. It should come with a disclaimer. Those who think they’re in for a mellifluous drama will be terribly disappointed. In fact, there are moments when you forget you are watching a movie at all. It feels like real life unfolding right in front of you, except that you are not just watching from the sidelines. You are actually in it. And that is what makes “Enjoy Your Stay” so unsettling. As the opening film of Cinemalaya 22, it was quite a statement. You don’t see films like this made every day. Directed by Dominik Locher and Honeylyn Joy Alipio, the film follows Luz (Mercedes Cabral), an undocumented Filipina cleaner working in a luxury Swiss ski resort while trying to keep custody of her daughter in Manila. The film takes us away from postcard Switzerland and into the lives of Filipino workers who exist mostly in the background of that beautiful world. They work, struggle, make mistakes and try to survive. There are no cartoonish villains here, nor are there heroes conveniently waiting to save the day. There are just ordinary people, each carrying their own dreams and aspirations, trying to claw their way toward a better life. And Luz is caught right in the middle of it. She has problems of her own, but her moral compass makes it difficult for her to simply go along with what everyone else is doing. You can feel her frustration. Her hopelessness. Her desperation. And that is where the film really gets you. Watching Luz make difficult choices is uncomfortable because you understand, at least to some extent, why she is making them. In a brief conversation, Cabral admitted that the role took a lot out of her. “Matagal bago ko napagpag ang character, mahirap,” she told us. The preparation more so. It did not help that she was preparing for the film while working on “FPJ’s Batang Quiapo.” “Mahaba ang proseso nito and I’m thankful na 'yung coaches na binigay nila sa kin were really helpful so, kahit hirap sa schedule I was able to prepare pa rin.” You can tell she understood what the film was trying to say. “Oo, kaya nga hopefully mas marami ang makanood na kababayan natin.” We hope so, too. Because this is the kind of film that makes you stop and think about people who leave home, often without proper documents, because they believe there is a better life waiting somewhere else. But what happens to them when things go wrong? And what is government really doing to protect people who have become so desperate that they are willing to risk everything just to have a fighting chance? It is an uncomfortable question because we know why undocumented migrants do what they do. They are not necessarily chasing a glamorous life. More often than not, they are simply trying to survive. “Enjoy Your Stay” does not make it easy to look away. For a while, you are among these people. You feel their fear. You share their desperation. You become frustrated with them and, sometimes, even for them. It is a difficult watch, yes. But strangely enough, we found ourselves thanking serendipity for allowing us to experience it. Because every once in a while, a film comes along that opens a door to a world most of us know little about. This is one of those films. And if it makes more people think about the lives of migrant workers, the risks they take and the systems that leave them vulnerable, then perhaps its discomfort is precisely the point. Cinemalaya 22 carries the theme “Reel Reflections.” “Enjoy Your Stay” certainly gives us something to reflect on.

Bam Aquino bats for monthly P2,000 support allowance for PWDs. Senator Bam Aquino is pushing for the creation of a monthly P2,000 disability support allowance for persons with disabilities (PWDs) to help them cover additional costs associated with their condition. Under Senate Bill (SB) No. 2386, or the National Disability Support Act, qualified PWDs would receive the allowance through a proposed National Disability Support Allowance Program. The benefit would also be periodically adjusted based on inflation to ensure that its value is maintained over time. “Persons with disabilities face additional and often invisible expenses in their daily lives, including transportation, healthcare, personal assistance, and assistive devices. These are essential not only for survival, but for participation in school, work, and community life. When these expenses are not addressed, opportunities are limited, poverty is deepened, and exclusion persists,” Aquino said. “This allowance is designed to complement existing social protection programs and empower persons with disabilities to live more independently, pursue education and employment, and participate more actively in society,” he added. The proposed program would be implemented in phases. For its first three years, the program would prioritize children with disabilities and adults with significant disabilities. Coverage would then be expanded during the succeeding three years to include PWDs with moderate disabilities who incur disability-related expenses. Eventually, all eligible PWDs who face additional costs because of their disabilities would be covered by the program. “By strengthening income support, this measure helps ensure that persons with disabilities are not only supported, but empowered to live independently and participate fully in society,” said Aquino, who stressed that greater support for PWDs would contribute to a more inclusive and equitable Philippines. The bill also proposes the establishment of a Disability and Needs Assessment System (DNAS) to determine eligibility. Instead of relying solely on income, the system would assess an individual's functional limitations, support requirements and barriers to participation. Aquino's measure further calls for the creation of a Disability Management Information System (DMIS), which would be connected to existing government databases such as the National ID System, the Philippine Persons with Disabilities Registry, PhilHealth and community-based monitoring systems. The system is intended to improve the government's disability data, support policymaking and service delivery, and enable the direct release of benefits to qualified recipients. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) would oversee the program, with assistance from a Multi-Stakeholder Committee headed by the National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA). “In empowering persons with disabilities, we are not only addressing inequality, but also unlocking potential, strengthening communities, and building a more inclusive and equitable Philippines,” Aquino said.

Keeping the momentum: How NEO’s existing buildings continue to lead in sustainable real estate. Across seven certified green office buildings in Bonifacio Global City, NEO is showing that existing and established properties can remain efficient, resilient, people-centered, and competitive through continuous investment and improvement. Sustainability in real estate is often associated with new buildings. But as cities continue to grow around properties that have already been built, an equally important question emerges: How can existing buildings continue to perform sustainably over time? NEO is showing that age does not have to limit a building’s environmental performance, workplace quality, or long-term competitiveness. The company owns, develops, and manages seven certified green office buildings in Bonifacio Global City, with a combined gross floor area of 256,707 square meters. Several of these properties have been operating for more than two decades, yet the portfolio continues to perform through regular upgrades, careful operations, proactive maintenance, and steady investment. Since shifting its entire portfolio to off-site renewable energy in 2013, NEO has expanded its sustainability efforts beyond energy management and conservation. Today, its approach covers water conservation, waste circularity, occupant health and well-being, resilience, connectivity, community engagement, and transparent governance. Rather than treating sustainability as a standard achieved once, NEO uses it as a framework for continuously improving how its buildings are managed, experienced, and prepared for the future. “Old and existing assets can deliver on multiple fronts—from zero carbon and health and safety to waste, community, and resilience.”— Raymond Rufino, Chief Executive Officer, NEO Measurable progress, even with higher occupancy The performance of an existing building is best demonstrated by how it improves over time. In 2025, average tenant occupancy across NEO’s portfolio increased from 94.5% to 95.94%. Despite more people using its buildings, NEO reduced emissions from building operations by 14.46%, electricity consumption by 1.74%, and water consumption by 3.17% across the portfolio compared with 2024. These improvements were supported by ongoing building optimization, conservation programs, performance monitoring, preventive maintenance, and tenant participation. For businesses, efficient building operations offer value beyond environmental targets. They can support more reliable services, better-managed operating costs, improved workplace conditions, and closer alignment with corporate sustainability commitments. For property owners, continuous improvement helps established assets remain attractive and competitive alongside newer developments. NEO’s portfolio has also earned recognized local and international sustainability credentials covering green building performance, zero carbon, occupant well-being, resilience, and digital connectivity. These include 5-Star BERDE and Advancing Net Zero Philippines certifications from the Philippine Green Building Council; EDGE Zero Carbon certification and A+ Building Resilience Index ratings from the International Finance Corporation (IFC); WELL Health-Safety and WELL Equity Ratings; and WiredScore certifications. Its EDGE performance further demonstrates what retrofitting can achieve in existing properties, with energy savings ranging from 41% to 48%, water savings of 44% to 56%, and reductions of 83% to 98% in embodied energy in materials. Together, these results show that sustainable real estate is not defined only during design and construction. It is also shaped by how effectively a building is operated, upgraded, and continuously improved throughout its life. Rethinking waste through circularity Improving an existing building also means looking beyond electricity and water use. It requires examining what happens to the materials and waste generated within the workplace. One of NEO’s priorities in 2025 was to reduce dependence on landfills while giving tenants more practical ways to participate in responsible waste management. Through its partnership with HMR Envirocycle Philippines, NEO introduced an electronic-waste recycling program across all seven buildings. Designated collection points allow tenants to properly dispose of end-of-life mobile phones, computers, chargers, and other electronic equipment through a convenient and traceable channel. The collected items are processed by an accredited recycling partner, ensuring that hazardous components are handled responsibly while usable materials are recovered and returned to formal recycling streams. NEO also partnered with Holcim Philippines through Geocycle to address residual waste that can no longer be reused or recycled through conventional methods. Instead of being sent to landfills, qualified materials are co-processed as alternative fuel or raw material for cement manufacturing. Through this collaboration, NEO became the first in the Philippine private real estate sector to adopt cement-kiln co-processing for post-consumer waste in partnership with Holcim. The two programs address different parts of the waste stream, but they reflect the same objective: making circularity part of everyday building operations. For tenants, these initiatives provide accessible ways to support responsible disposal and resource recovery within the workplace. For NEO, they strengthen waste diversion, reduce landfill dependency, and promote more efficient use of resources across the portfolio. Healthy workplaces are sustainable workplaces Buildings are ultimately used and experienced by people. Their long-term value depends not only on resource efficiency, but also on whether occupants feel healthy, safe, included, and supported in the places where they work. Through the implementation of WELL at Scale across its portfolio, NEO’s health and well-being strategies now reach more than 27,500 building occupants. All seven buildings achieved WELL Health-Safety and WELL Equity Ratings. In 2025, NEO was also recognized with the WELL Health and Safety Leadership Award, Equity Leadership Award, and WELL Community Award. These programs cover areas such as indoor environmental quality, health and well-being support, inclusion, emergency preparedness, community engagement, and responsible building operations. By embedding these measures into everyday property management, NEO treats occupant health and safety as outcomes that must be monitored and continuously improved. The company further strengthened emergency preparedness through its partnership with Lifeline. A dedicated ambulance coverage system provides coordinated emergency medical support across NEO’s seven-building portfolio, complementing existing security procedures, emergency drills, occupational health measures, and building safety systems. For tenants and their employees, this creates greater confidence in the workplace. Reliable building operations, timely emergency response, and proactive preparedness also contribute to business continuity and long-term organizational resilience. Extending impact beyond the workplace NEO’s sustainability efforts are not limited to the physical performance of its buildings. The company also uses its portfolio as a platform for tenant participation, environmental action, education, and community engagement. In partnership with WWF-Philippines, NEO organized a coastal clean-up at the Las Piñas–Parañaque Critical Habitat and Ecotourism Area. The activity brought together 71 employee and tenant volunteers, who collected 116 sacks of waste weighing 574 kilograms. Tenant volunteers joined the activity for the first time in 2025, contributing to a 25% increase in participation compared with the previous year. Their involvement reflects NEO’s broader goal of turning sustainability into a shared responsibility among building owners, property teams, tenants, and employees. NEO also collaborated with students, instructors, and the Sisters from The Sisters of Mary School on a mural program across its properties. Inspired by Philippine landmarks, cultural heritage, and national identity, the artworks transformed selected building spaces into visual expressions of creativity and local pride. Following the project, NEO donated drawing tablets to participating students to support their continued development in both traditional and digital art. While different in form, the WWF and Sisters of Mary initiatives demonstrate how established buildings can create value beyond their physical boundaries. They can become places where environmental awareness, creativity, learning, and community participation are encouraged. Accountability and resilience As a privately held and non-listed company, NEO is not required to publish a sustainability report. It continues to do so because it considers transparency and accountability essential to long-term progress. This commitment received international recognition in 2025 when NEO was awarded the Grand Award for Best Sustainability Report—Non-Listed Company and received a commendation for the Carbon Neutral Award at the Hong Kong ESG Reporting Awards. NEO was also included in the Greater Bay Area Outstanding ESG Disclosure List. These recognitions affirm the quality of NEO’s disclosures, its approach to climate accountability, and its efforts to communicate measurable sustainability performance. Resilience is equally important to the continued performance of its existing buildings. NEO’s A+ Building Resilience Index rating is supported by preventive maintenance, regular testing of critical equipment and building systems, business continuity planning, emergency exercises, and coordination with organizations such as the Bureau of Fire Protection, the Bonifacio Global City Estates Association, and Lifeline. For businesses located within the portfolio, this focus on preparedness helps reduce operational risk and supports safer, more reliable working environments. For NEO, it strengthens the long-term relevance and competitiveness of properties that must continue adapting to changing environmental, operational, and tenant requirements. Keeping existing buildings ready for what comes next NEO’s sustainability journey continues in 2026. Its priorities include pursuing WELL certifications across the portfolio, working toward a 4-Star GRESB rating, increasing waste diversion from landfills, beginning the management of indirect emissions generated across its broader value chain, and expanding the NEO Green Team to achieve majority employee participation across departments. These next steps reinforce a long-term approach centered on continually improving existing assets rather than viewing sustainability as a completed milestone. For tenants, this means workplaces that remain aligned with evolving expectations around efficiency, employee experience, safety, resilience, and responsible business practices. For the broader real estate industry, it provides an example of how established properties can continue to contribute to sustainable urban development. By proving that existing buildings can continue to improve, adapt, and lead, NEO is helping expand the meaning of sustainable real estate—one that is measured not only by how buildings are designed, but by how they are managed, experienced, and continuously improved over time. This is #theNEOway: keeping the momentum by improving the performance of existing buildings, helping communities thrive, and enabling businesses to grow more responsibly.

Man nabbed for phone theft, child abuse; used own photo as wallpaper. A 25-year-old man was arrested after allegedly entering a house uninvited in Barangay Pinagbuhatan, Pasig City, where he inappropriately touched a child before stealing a mobile phone. Authorities said the incident occurred on the night of Aug. 5. The suspect, identified as “Yekyek,” allegedly touched an intimate area of the sleeping 8-year-old girl inside the house before taking the victim’s mobile phone. The victim woke up and immediately reported the incident to her mother, while the suspect fled the house. The victim’s family immediately reported the incident to the barangay. CCTV footage from inside the house led authorities to identify the suspect, who reportedly also lived in the area and was later arrested. During his arrest, the victim’s mobile phone was recovered, with the suspect’s own photo set as the wallpaper. Authorities added that suspected shabu was also recovered from him. The suspect is now in the custody of the Pasig City Police Station and will face charges of theft, acts of lasciviousness, and violation of the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act.

David Licauco reacts to Barbie Forteza’s ‘ideal leading man’ comment on Khalil Ramos. David Licauco was asked recently about Barbie Forteza’s praise for Khalil Ramos, whom she described as her “ideal leading man.” His response was brief. “That’s her opinion, it’s okay,” Licauco said. Forteza made the remark while talking about her experience working with Ramos in her latest film "Saving Cherry." “Si Khalil is the ideal leading man. Finally, nagkaroon na ako ng leading man na maayos,” she said, describing him as a brilliant actor, professional and gentlemanly. The statement drew attention because of Forteza’s long partnership with Licauco. The two became one of GMA’s most popular love teams after playing Fidel and Klay in “Maria Clara at Ibarra.” They later worked together in “Maging Sino Ka Man,” “Pulang Araw” and the movie “That Kind of Love.” Licauco was given a chance to respond to Forteza’s assessment, but did not appear interested in making an issue out of it. “Masyado nang marami nangyayari sa mundo, dapat magmahalan at magsuportahan na lang tayo,” he said. As if eager to prove his claim, he went on to laud Forteza. “I am grateful sa partnership namin. I have nothing but praise for her. Napakagaling niyang actress. I wish her well,” he said. Taking stock of his years with BarDa, he admitted there were things he could have done better. “Maybe not perfect. There were times na I was late sa taping. But habang tumatagal yung love team at pinagsamahan namin, hindi naman ako naging late. In terms of acting, okay naman, I guess. May awards naman ako.” Licauco recently signed a series contract with Viva Films in partnership with ALV Talent Circuit.

VP Sara: Bring ‘bayanihan’ to the global stage, empower ASEAN youth. Emphasizing that unity, cooperation, and a common vision are key to building a stronger and more resilient regional community, Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday, Aug. 8, urged Southeast Asians to bring the Filipino spirit of “bayanihan” to the global stage and challenged ASEAN's youth to help shape the region's shared future as the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) celebrated its 59th anniversary. In her ASEAN Day message released by the Office of the Vice President (OVP), Duterte emphasized the importance of regional solidarity and cooperation, describing ASEAN as a diverse community bound by shared aspirations. "Home to nearly 700 million people, our region is a vibrant tapestry of different cultures, languages, and dreams," Duterte said. She stressed that ASEAN's common objective is to create "a future where every young person can thrive, no matter where they come from." Drawing from her experience as former president of the Southeast Asian Ministers of Education Organization (SEAMEO) Council, Duterte underscored the value of collaboration among Southeast Asian nations. She likened regional cooperation to the Filipino tradition of “bayanihan,” where an entire community works together to move a neighbor's house to safety. "This is exactly how we must build our shared future. No country carries the weight alone. We lift each other up," she said. As ASEAN celebrates 59 years of regional partnership, Duterte urged member states to bring the same spirit of “bayanihan” to the global stage through stronger cooperation and mutual support. She also challenged the region's young people to take an active role in shaping ASEAN's future. "I challenge our ASEAN youth to conquer challenges in shaping our shared future, united by our shared vision, and driven by our shared purpose," Duterte said.

Lexus unveiled all-new ES. Recognizing a renewed appreciation for executive sedans, Lexus Philippines has officially launched the all-new ES. The latest generation is a complete redesign and reflects the brand's vision for the future of luxury mobility, combining electrified performance, intuitive technology, and elevated comfort. The all-new ES introduces Lexus' latest design gives the executive sedan a more commanding yet elegant presence. It features a sleek fastback-inspired silhouette and a reinterpreted spindle grille. It also rides on a 2,950-mm wheelbase, creating a spacious cabin while contributing to greater ride stability and refinement. Hybrid and EV The new ES is offered in two powertrains as part of its multi-pathway approach to electrification, offering customers the flexibility to choose the powertrain that best complements their lifestyle. The first is the ES 350h is powered by a 2.5-liter inline four-cylinder hybrid powertrain producing 247-PS. The hybrid system preserves the quiet ride quality and seamless driving experience that are hallmarks of the Lexus ES. Making its Philippine debut is the ES 350e Battery Electric Vehicle, the country's first fully electric Lexus ES. Powered by a 74.69-kWh lithium-ion battery, the ES 350e develops 224 PS and offers an estimated 493 kilometers of driving range under the WLTP testing standard. The vehicle supports both Type 2 AC charging and CCS2 DC fast charging, providing greater convenience for daily commuting and longer journeys alike. Inside, the cabin design of the all-new ES continues Lexus' philosophy of Omotenashi — the Japanese principle of anticipating the needs of every guest. Every element of the cabin has been thoughtfully designed to create an environment that feels welcoming, intuitive, and effortlessly luxurious. Whether hybrid or electric, a new 14-inch touchscreen display serves as the centerpiece of the cabin, providing seamless access to vehicle functions, navigation, and connectivity features. Every variant also comes equipped with a panoramic tilt-and-slide sunroof, creating a greater sense of openness for both driver and passengers. Crafted around Omotenashi The ES 350h is split into two variants, the Executive and Luxury. The Executive variant features synthetic leather upholstery paired with a 10-speaker audio system, delivering premium comfort as standard. The ES 350h Luxury elevates the experience with perforated synthetic leather seating and a 17-speaker Mark Levinson Premium Surround Sound System, surrounding occupants with concert-quality audio. At the top of the range, the ES 350e combines semi-aniline leather upholstery, the 17-speaker Mark Levinson audio system, and Adaptive Variable Suspension (AVS) to create the most refined and engaging ES driving experience yet. Exclusive 21-inch alloy wheels further distinguish the flagship model while complementing its enhanced dynamic performance. Subtle differences are also ecident on the exterior. The ES 350h Executive and ES 350h Luxury features newly designed 19-inch Aero alloy wheels, while the flagship ES 350e Battery Electric Vehicle is distinguished by exclusive 21-inch Luxury alloy wheels, reinforcing its premium character. Complementing the exterior is a sophisticated selection of finishes, led by Sou, a newly introduced color. Customers may also choose from Sonic Copper, Sonic Titanium, Sonic Chrome, Sonic Iridium, White Nova Glass Flake, and Graphite Black Glass Flake, allowing every ES to reflect its owner's individual style. High tech safety Safety remains central to the Lexus experience. Every All-New ES comes equipped with Lexus Safety System+ 4, the brand's latest suite of advanced driver assistance technologies designed to support the driver across a wide range of everyday driving situations. Parking and low-speed maneuvering are equally enhanced. The ES 350h Executive is equipped with a Back Guide Monitor, while the ES 350h Luxury and ES 350e feature a Panoramic View Monitor, providing greater visibility of the vehicle's surroundings for added confidence behind the wheel. The All-New Lexus ES is available in three electrified variants. The ES 350h Executive is priced at P4,108,000; The ES 350h Luxury is priced at P4,308,000. The ES 350e Battery Electric Vehicle is priced at P5,688,000. The all-new Lexus ES lineup is now available for viewing and test drive at the Lexus Gallery in Bonifacio Global City.

‘Don’t shoot first’: Alan Cayetano defends Taguig lakeshore amid feud with Lacson. Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano on Friday defended the lakeshore development in Taguig City amid criticism from fellow Senator Panfilo Lacson, as he said the project was intended to protect Laguna Lake and benefit the public. In a Facebook livestream, Cayetano said the development was designed to protect the lake, provide spaces for public use, and prevent areas along the lakeshore from being occupied by informal settlers or taken over by private interests. He said the project had undergone changes under different administrations and that its purpose should be understood by examining its history and consulting officials involved in its planning and implementation. “The purpose po is to protect the lake. Ang purpose po ay ma-enjoy ng tao. Ang purpose po ay hindi malagyan ng informal settlers at hindi po magkaroon po ng mga, or kung hindi man informal settlers, hindi magkaroon ng mga sindikato, na kakamkamin ang mga lupa dyan at gagawin private (The purpose is to protect the lake. The purpose is for people to enjoy it. The purpose is to prevent informal settlers from occupying it and, if not informal settlers, to prevent syndicates from taking over the land and turning it into private property),” Cayetano said. Cayetano also highlighted the project's benefits to Taguig residents. He says around 1.3 million people in the city and hundreds of thousands of nearby residents use the roads and public spaces developed along the lakeshore. He urged critics to first seek clarification from the appropriate officials rather than immediately raising allegations of irregularities. “Don't shoot first then ask questions later,” Cayetano said, and added that discussions should begin by examining the development of the Taguig lakeshore and its flood-control infrastructure. The Senate minority leader also pushed back against any suggestion that he was preventing Lacson from investigating corruption. “Kailan ko po siya pinigilan na labanan niya po yung mga korap? Siya po ang biglang tumigil sa mga imbestigasyon (When did I ever stop him from going after corrupt individuals? He was the one who suddenly stopped the investigations),” Cayetano said. At the same time, Cayetano said public officials should remain open to scrutiny and investigations. Political positions, he stressed, should not dictate how issues are handled. “All of us deserve the benefit of the doubt but all of us should be open to any investigation,” he said. Cayetano said he would continue to stand up for the public while taking a case-by-case approach to government issues rather than being “totally anti-admin” or “totally pro-admin". The senator also cited his long involvement in Taguig, and said he has been working in the city since 1992 and acknowledging that he and the local government were not perfect. “Life's work na po namin yan (That's our life's work). We're not perfect. Like any other local government, like any other public official, may mga pagkukulang din kami (we have shortcomings),” Cayetano said. He said the focus should ultimately remain on determining the truth, and that political criticism and scrutiny were normal in public life.

TV5 bets on nostalgia, fresh dramas and Korina Sanchez as network unveils second-half slate. TV5 is leaning on nostalgia, familiar faces and new local dramas as it rolls out its programming lineup for the second half of 2026. At its “Tara, Kapatid!” Midyear Media and Trade Celebration on Aug. 6, the network announced a slate of programs that includes the return of veteran broadcaster Korina Sanchez-Roxas to a bigger role, a reunion of stars who defined late-1990s Philippine television and several new primetime dramas. One of the biggest announcements was “Mommy Guard,” a new series that brings together Marvin Agustin, Jolina Magdangal and Dominic Ochoa nearly three decades after they first became household names through projects including “Gimik” and the hit film “Hey Babe!” The series, which premieres in September, will be directed by Roman Perez Jr. Details about the story remain under wraps. Magdangal said the production is aware of the nostalgia surrounding their reunion, but noted that the interest is not limited to longtime fans. “We understand na ‘yung appeal of this is ‘yung nostalgia factor, pero nagulat ako na marami na ring mga bagong henerasyon na natutuwa sa tambalan namin. Siguro ‘yung mga anak ng fans namin,” she said. Agustin and Magdangal became one of the defining love teams of the late 1990s, while Ochoa was also a familiar face from “Gimik” and the Whattamen trio. “I’m just so excited to reunite with Jolina and, of course, Dominic. It’s always fun to work with them and I hope na magustuhan ninyo ang palabas namin,” Agustin said. TV5 is also giving Sanchez-Roxas a larger presence on the network. Her daily talk show, “Face to Face with Ate Koring,” anchors the late-morning block, while “Rated Korina” continues on weekends. Speaking on the sidelines of the event, Sanchez-Roxas said the revamped “Face to Face” has moved away from the explosive confrontations that became associated with its earlier run. “It’s lighter now. We still tackle real issues, but there are also inspiring stories, extraordinary children, celebrities and trending topics that people can learn from,” she said. She also credited the show’s sidekicks, DJ Laila Chikadora and Cheena Crab, for bringing a more relaxed energy to the program. Sanchez-Roxas also brushed aside suggestions that she could be overexposed with five programs airing across different platforms. “No,” she said. “If people continue watching, it means they like what you’re doing.” Beyond the returning stars, TV5 is adding to its primetime offerings with “Sigabo,” “A Secret in Prague” starring Andrea Brillantes, and “My Bespren Emman.”

Gilas, China in early collision course as Asiad grouping unveiled. Gilas Pilipinas is set for an early collision course with powerhouse China after being drawn together in the Group C of the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games men’s 5-on-5 basketball tournament. The Asian Games Organizing Committee officially unveiled the groups on Friday, Aug. 7, with the 12 teams participating divided into three groups. Gilas, the defending champion of the tournament after ruling the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou, are grouped with China, Bahrain and Kazakhstan. Host Japan is in Group A along with South Korea, Saudi Arabia and Indonesia while Group B has contenders Iran and Jordan together with Chinese Taipei and Qatar. The Nationals will open their campaign against Bahrain on Sept. 11 before taking on Kazakhstan the following day. Gilas will play China on the final day of the group stage on Sept. 14 with Team Dragon also surely raring to get back at Gilas after the Filipinos defeated the Chinese, 77-76, right on its home turf. Aside from the contest having big implications given the two teams’ history and respective campaigns, the clash is also expected to draw attention from fans as the match comes against the backdrop of the continuing territorial dispute between the two countries. The Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas has already submitted the initial long list for the continental meet with Justin Brownlee, who poured in 17 of his 33 points – including two back-breaking triples against China in the semifinals, expected to once again spearhead Gilas. Other naturalized players Bennie Boatwright and Ange Kouame are also part of the pool which is mostly composed of PBA players. Gilas mainstays Kai Sotto, Dwight Ramos, AJ Edu, Quentin Millora-Brown, Mike Phillips. CJ Perez, Scottie Thompson, RJ Abarrientos, Troy Rosario, Calvin Oftana, Juan Gomez de Liano, Justine Baltazar and Chris Newsome are still named to the pool. Ramos and Edu, however, have already been ruled out by SBP executive director Erika Dy due to their B.League commitments. Also part of the pool are Jamie Malonzo, Jerrick Ahanmisi, Don Trollano, Jordan Heading, Brandon Ganuelas-Rosser, Justin Arana, Adrian Nocum, Caelan Tiongson, Brandon Bates, Sedrick Barefield, Robert Bolick, Zavier Lucero and Jason Perkins.

Eala outlasts McNally, storms into fourth round in Toronto. Alex Eala dug deep to outlast a gritty Caty McNally, 6-3, 5-7, 6-4, and storm into the fourth round of the 2026 National Bank Open in Toronto, Canada on Saturday, Aug. 8 (Philippine time). The 25th-seeded Filipina battled through a nagging left-ankle issue that required a medical timeout in the second set before holding her nerve in the deciding third frame to seal the hard-fought victory in two hours and 39 minutes. After sealing match point, Eala was overcome with emotion and nearly burst into tears as the fatigue finally set in. She then walked to the middle of the court to exchange handshakes with McNally in a show of sportsmanship. Eala credited McNally for pushing her to the limit throughout the marathon battle. “I think I survived that one. It was so tough. I want to thank Caty for a great match, being a great sport. It’s one of those matches that really could have gone either way,” said Eala. “I think it was really down to details and a little bit of luck,” she added. The win marked Eala’s seventh straight victory since her breakthrough WTA Tour title at the Mubadala DC Open in Washington, D.C. last week. It also set up another stern test for Eala against former world No. 4 and 12th seed Belinda Bencic, who likewise survived a grueling battle with Taylor Townsend, 6-7 (5), 7-6 (4), 6-4. The seasoned Swiss star brings an imposing resume, having twice reached the Grand Slam semifinals and captured the gold medal at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics. Against McNally, who came into the match brimming with confidence after stunning reigning Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, 7-5 (5), 6-1, Eala capitalized on seven break-point conversions against the hard-hitting American. The Filipina battled back from a 1-3 deficit, rattling off five straight games to seize the opening set. But a nagging left-ankle issue disrupted her momentum, forcing her to call for a medical timeout while leading 3-2. McNally grew more aggressive after the break, turning a 4-5 deficit into a set win to force a decider. But Eala soldiered on in the third, breaking McNally’s serve in the opening game before holding her own and steadily pulling away to seal the match win.

CJ Gesmundo: Distinct roles of judiciary, media in upholding rule of law. Chief Justice Alexander G. Gesmundo underscored the distinct roles of the judiciary and the media in strengthening public understanding of the principles and confidence in institutions that uphold the rule of law. He said that both the judiciary and the media rely on confidence that comes from faithfully fulfilling their respective responsibilities. “The judiciary earns that confidence through the fair and impartial administration of justice; the media earns it through responsible journalism and fidelity to truth,” he pointed out. The Chief Justice was guest speaker during the “Judiciary Night” event of the Manila Overseas Press Club (MOPC) held in Makati City last Friday night, August 7. He recalled that the Supreme Court (SC) has been serving as the guardian of the Constitution, the protector of rights and liberties, and the final arbiter of legal disputes affecting our nation. He pointed out that “through periods of transformation, uncertainty, and challenge, the Court has remained committed to preserving the constitutional order and the rule of law.” “But the enduring value of an institution is reflected not only in the legacy it inherits, but also in its capacity for renewal. For the Judiciary, renewal means safeguarding judicial independence while continuously improving the administration of justice. It means ensuring that courts remain not only independent, but also efficient, accessible, and responsive to the needs of the people,” he said. Gesmundo recalled that three years ago, he was guest speaker during MOPC’s “Judiciary Night” and tackled the SC’s Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovations 2022–2027 (SPJI). “Today, the SPJI serves as the framework guiding the Judiciary’s continuing efforts toward institutional improvement. It has provided direction for reforms designed to strengthen judicial integrity, enhance court efficiency, expand access to justice, and modernize the delivery of judicial services,” he said. He pointed out that the purpose of the innovations and reforms is to make the justice system responsive to the needs and realities of the Filipinos. Since the foundation of all efforts is integrity, the judiciary has continued to strengthen the mechanisms that promote accountability and professionalism throughout the justice system, he said. Also, he said the SC adopted the Code of Judicial Conduct and Accountability and the Code of Conduct and Accountability for Court Officials and Employees as the court “recognizes that the delivery of justice depends not only on the decisions issued by judges, but also on the dedication, professionalism, and ethical conduct of every person who forms part of the Judiciary.” He emphasized that the dignity and credibility of the judiciary are preserved not only in the courtroom, “but also in every act of service performed in the name of justice.” At the same time, Gesmundo cited the SC’s continuing efforts to modernize its processes and expand access to judicial services since “justice cannot remain distant from the people who need it most.” He cited initiatives such as eCourt PH 2.0, electronic filing and service, digital records management, and other technological innovations to make court processes more efficient and accessible. He also cited the use of artificial intelligence through Scriptix, an AI-assisted transcription software that significantly reduces the time needed to prepare court transcripts from weeks to days, allowing court personnel to focus on more essential judicial work. Thereafter, he said the Rules on Electronic Notarization will soon allow the electronic notarization of digital documents anywhere in the country, making notarization more convenient and accessible. To improve access to legal information, Gesmundo said the SC launched the Philippine Reports E-Books on the Supreme Court E-Library, enabling lawyers, judges, law students, researchers, and the public to access the court’s official decisions anytime and anywhere. He also cited the Rules on Unified Legal Aid Services (ULAS), the free legal service to indigent Filipinos. Through ULAS, lawyers are mandated to render at least 60 hours of free legal service every three years to indigent Filipinos. In its earlier press statement, the MOPC described Gesmundo as “a reformist jurist, one rich in knowledge and practice of law, skilled in the administration of a complex and labyrinthine system that is the judiciary, imbued with enormous integrity and independence and yet keenly attuned to the needs of people who have less in law, less in life and less in the dignity that all men are entitled to.” Chief Justice Gesmundo will retire on Nov. 6, 2026 when he reaches the mandatory retirement age of 70. He was appointed SC associate justice on Aug. 14, 2017 and as chief justice on April 5, 2021. He said: “As my service as Chief Justice draws to a close, I do so with a deep sense of gratitude and humility. The opportunity to serve as Chief Justice has never been a personal distinction. It has been a responsibility sustained each day by the dedication of countless individuals who quietly perform the work of justice across the country. “Looking back on this journey, one lesson stands above all others: the strength of the Judiciary has never rested on the efforts of any single individual. It rests on the collective commitment of those who carry out its mission- on justices and judges who decide with courage and fairness, on court officials and employees who perform their duties with dedication and professionalism, on lawyers who uphold their responsibilities as officers of the court, on our partners in government, civil society, academe, and the media who contribute to the continuing work of strengthening the rule of law, and on citizens who come before our courts believing that justice will be administered fairly, impartially, and with respect for their rights and dignity. “The Judiciary does not belong to any one person, administration, or generation. It belongs to the Constitution and, ultimately, to the Filipino people whom it serves.”

Audi RS5 Avant PHEV blends performance with sustainability. The all-new Audi RS 5 Avant PHEV is now in the Philippines. Other RS hallmarks include a sports exhaust system, and a sport suspension with controlled 2-valve dampers. Inside, the RS 5 Avant PHEV gets the Audi Sport seat plus wrapped in fine nappa leather, trimmed with honeycomb patterns and contrast stitching. Vegan PDRN vs. salmon PDRN: What a dermatologist wants you to know. With science continuously reshaping the beauty industry, one skincare ingredient has quickly become one of K-beauty's biggest exports: PDRN or polydeoxyribonucleotide. Traditionally derived from salmon DNA, the ingredient has gained popularity for its role in regenerative treatments and skincare, appearing in everything from injectable procedures to topical products. As the category continues to evolve, plant-based alternatives are beginning to emerge. On Aug. 25, Dermlab+ by Fresh introduced its new Lumi Rejucare skincare line, combining rose vegan PDRN with Cica exosome in a cleanser, toner, and cream designed for everyday use. Salmon-derived vs vegan PDRN During the launch held at Whitespace Makati, board-certified dermatologist Dr. Bea Chan-Benavidez explained why vegan PDRN may have an advantage over topical salmon-derived versions. According to Dr. Bea, PDRN consists of DNA fragments that act as biosignaling molecules, helping strengthen the skin barrier, support cellular regeneration, and provide deep hydration. While traditional salmon-derived PDRN has been shown to be effective when administered through injections, she said topical versions face a challenge. "Their main limiting factor comes from the fact that you can't absorb them topically," she explained. Rose vegan PDRN, on the other hand, is 200 times smaller than traditional salmon-derived PDRN, making it easier for the skin to absorb. Better absorption, she said, could translate to faster results. The new line also combines vegan PDRN with Cica exosome, which packages centella asiatica into nano-sized carrier vesicles to help the ingredient penetrate deeper into the skin. According to her, this combination helps calm inflammation, including redness, itching, and swelling, while supporting collagen production in as fast as two months. The formula also contains alpha arbutin for gentle brightening and saccharide isomerate, a biomimetic humectant that binds to the skin to provide up to 72 hours of hydration. Together, she said, these ingredients address what she considers the three pillars of healthy skin: a resilient skin barrier, even-looking skin tone, and long-lasting hydration. Dr. Bea also pointed out that plant-derived ingredients offer additional benefits, including being eco-friendly, cruelty-free, and less likely to trigger allergic reactions. She added that vegan rose PDRN is suitable for all skin types, including sensitive skin, although she still recommends consulting a board-certified dermatologist before starting a new skincare routine. She also debunked the notion that PDRN is only for mature skin. "When we talk about cellular regeneration or healing, we are referring to an environment that fosters repair and recovery of your cells," she said. "No matter your age, you will benefit from using vegan rose PDRN because it helps build a stronger skin barrier, calm skin sensitivity, and fade hyperpigmentation." New addition to Rei Germar’s routine Also introduced during the event was content creator Rei Germar as the face of the campaign. A long-time Fresh user, Rei said she appreciated that the new collection allows users to incorporate PDRN into their existing skincare routine instead of replacing it entirely. She also shared that among the three products, her favorite is the cream, describing it as lightweight and quickly absorbed, making it easy to layer with other products. As she approaches her 30s, Rei said skincare has become more focused on maintaining a healthy skin barrier than simply chasing anti-aging products. "It's never too early for anti-aging and barriers," she said. "Here in the Philippines, not a lot of people talk about their skin barrier and how a lot of things really affect it." She added that the collection fits her busy lifestyle because it offers a straightforward routine while incorporating trending ingredients such as PDRN and Cica exosome.

TCL NXTPAPER smartphone series arrives: A whole new way to experience your screen. For years, TCL has built its reputation as one of the world's leading TV brands, known for making premium display technology more accessible to consumers. Now, the global technology company is taking the next step in its evolution by officially unveiling its smartphone lineup, bringing its expertise in display innovation to mobile devices. Leading the launch are the NXTPAPER 60 Ultra, NXTPAPER 70 Pro, and K70 Power 4G—a new generation of smartphones designed to deliver smarter, more comfortable, and more powerful mobile experiences for today's connected lifestyle. At the heart of the lineup is TCL's proprietary NXTPAPER technology, an award-winning display innovation that redefines how people use their smartphones. First introduced in 2021, NXTPAPER combines hardware and software advancements to reduce eye strain while preserving vivid colors and sharp picture quality. The result is a paper-like viewing experience that remains comfortable even during extended hours of reading, working, streaming, or scrolling. "We're excited to officially introduce TCL Mobile Phones to the Philippine market. This launch reflects our commitment to bringing meaningful innovation to more consumers through devices that enhance the way people work, create, communicate, and stay entertained every day. KATSEYE hit by second health break as Sophia Laforteza steps away. KATSEYE is facing another unexpected shake-up as leader Sophia Laforteza becomes the second member of the global girl group to step away from activities this year for health reasons. HYBE x Geffen announced Friday, Aug. 7, that Sophia would temporarily sit out the group’s promotional activities to prioritize her mental health and overall well-being. The development comes about six months after Manon Bannerman also took a temporary hiatus, with the label saying at the time that she needed to focus on her health and well-being. Sophia’s case, however, comes with a more detailed explanation from management. “We are very sorry to share that Sophia will be temporarily unable to participate in upcoming promotional activities,” HYBE x Geffen said in a statement posted on Weverse. The label said Sophia has been receiving support and, following consultations with medical professionals, was advised to take an extended period of rest and continue receiving care to allow for a full recovery. “It is imperative that her mental health and wellness are prioritized,” the statement added. Sophia, who has emerged as one of KATSEYE’s most recognizable members and serves as the group’s leader, acknowledged that stepping away was difficult. “Making this decision wasn’t easy, but I’m learning that health has to come first,” she said in a message to fans. She explained that continuing to push herself without taking care of her mind and body could prevent her from doing what she loves in the long run. The timing makes the announcement particularly significant for KATSEYE, which has been building momentum with major performances and a packed schedule. With Manon still on temporary hiatus, Sophia’s absence means the group will now move forward with four members for its upcoming activities. HYBE x Geffen said Sophia wanted to continue participating despite her condition, but management chose to prioritize her health, safety and long-term well-being. The label plans to reassess her condition in September and provide fans with another update. For Sophia, the break is not a goodbye. “I promise I’m going to work as hard as I can to get through this, heal properly, and come back stronger,” she told EYEKONS.

'Mag-resign na lang kayo': Barbers has message for pro-China local officials. Former House quad-committee (quad-comm) overall chairman Robert Ace Barbers says local government officials who habitually favor the interests of China over the Philippines should simply resign. "The issue is not whether one is pro-China, pro-America, or aligned with any other foreign power. The only acceptable position for every public servant is to be unequivocally pro-Philippines," Barbers said in a statement on Saturday, Aug. 8. The current House impeachment adviser says his call covers both officials who are openly and covertly advocating positions that are consistently in favor of China over the Philippines. Barbers stressed that every government official--from the highest elective office to the lowest appointive position--took a solemn oath to preserve and defend the Constitution, protect the Republic, and faithfully serve the Filipino people. This oath, he said, cannot be reconciled with acts or pronouncements that undermine the country's sovereign rights, territorial integrity, or national interests. The moment a government official begins advancing the strategic interests of another country over those of our own, that official has betrayed the very essence of public service, he reckoned. “Public office demands one allegiance dahil hindi ito “dual citizenship” - isang bandila lang ang dapat pinaglingkuran mo at ‘yan ay kung sino ang nagpapa-sweldo sa yo.. an official of this govt requires undivided loyalty.” (Public office demands one allegiance because it is not “dual citizenship” — only one flag should be served, and that is the one who pays your salary. An official of this government requires undivided loyalty.) He says that during Mondays and Fridays--in all government offices and in all school levels--Filipinos are required to attend Flag Raising and Flag Retreat activities, respectively, and all “sing our National Anthem” with a vow of "dying for the country" in times of foreign invasion or aggression. The ex-solon from Surigao del Norte emphasized that his appeal was not directed at ordinary citizens who may hold differing opinions on foreign policy. “Rather it is addressed to government officials who occupy positions of public trust, where their words, decisions, and policy recommendations directly affect national security, diplomacy, and the welfare of the Filipino people,” he said. Barbers likewise underscored that calls for voluntary resignation, as pronounced publicly by Department of National Defense (DND) Secretary Gibo Teodoro, would help preserve the integrity of government institutions by eliminating any lingering doubts about possible conflicts between personal convictions and official responsibilities. “Public office demands not only competence but also the confidence of the people that government decisions are made exclusively in the national interest,” he said.

1 dead, over 26,000 affected by bad weather in La Union. ‎ SAN FERNANDO CITY, La Union — At least one person was reported dead while more than 26,000 individuals were affected by flooding, landslides, and other incidents in La Union due to the combined effects of the southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones Luis and Maymay. ‎ ‎The provincial disaster office said Saturday, Aug. 8, that the fatality was a 45-year-old man who drowned in an irrigation canal in Barangay Rimos 1, Luna. ‎ ‎As of 5 a.m. Saturday, the La Union Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (PDRRMO) recorded 46 flooding incidents in Bauang, Agoo, Bangar, Santo Tomas, Naguilian, and San Fernando City caused by Luis and Maymay. ‎ ‎Four landslides were recorded in Sudipen, Naguilian, and Luna, as well as two mudslides and one rockslide in San Fernando City. ‎ ‎A total of 8,366 families or 26,612 individuals in 192 barangays in 17 municipalities were affected by inclement weather. ‎ ‎Five-hundred eighty-eight families or 1,756 individuals are staying in 50 evacuation centers while 354 families or 1,161 individuals are staying outside evacuation centers. ‎ ‎Nineteen houses were partially damaged in San Fernando City, San Juan, Agoo, Bauang, Caba, Naguilian, and Santo Tomas and two totally in Bauang and Naguilian. ‎ ‎Local government units and the provincial government of La Union have provided assistance amounting to P913,981.24 to affected residents. ‎ ‎Initial damage assessment placed agricultural losses at P12.91 million, infrastructure damage at P3.4 million, and livestock losses at P205,950. ‎ ‎Authorities distributed 2,900 food packs to affected residents through 16 local government units. ‎ ‎The PDRRMO said damage assessment remains ongoing and the figures may still increase as reports from affected areas continue to be consolidated. ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎

‎PRO-NIR honors fallen cop for rescue attempt. ‎BACOLOD CITY - The Police Regional Office-Negros Island Region (PRO-NIR) honored the sacrifice of Police Master Sgt. Fernando Marfa who drowned while saving his three companions during a river patrol in Barangay Luna, Cadiz City, Negros Occidental on Friday, Aug. 7. ‎ "Marfa exemplified the true meaning of service above self. His final act was one of extraordinary courage, choosing to risk his own life to save others," said Police Brig. Gen. Romano Cardiño, PRO-NIR director. ‎ “We mourn the loss of a dedicated police officer, a brave public servant, and a hero,” Cardiño added. ‎ The PRO-NIR condoled with Marfa’s family and assured them that his sacrifice will always be remembered and honored. ‎ Cardiño said that Marfa’s selfless act of courage and unwavering commitment to protect and save others, even at the cost of his own life, embody the highest ideals of public service and the noblest traditions of the Philippine National Police (PNP). ‎ He said they remain steadfast in honoring the heroism and dedication of personnel who faithfully fulfill their sworn duty of protecting lives and serving the people, even in the face of great danger. ‎ Marfa was patrolling with members of the Bantay Dagat when river water entered their motorboat. Authorities say Brandon Clarke died from effects of heroin, cocaine. LOS ANGELES (AP) — Memphis Grizzlies forward Brandon Clarke died in May from the effects of heroin and cocaine, authorities said Friday, Aug. 7. The Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner said the 29-year-old basketball player's death was accidental. Clarke was found dead inside a home near Los Angeles on May 11. A person familiar with the terms of the investigation told The Associated Press after the Grizzlies announced Clarke’s passing that drug paraphernalia was found at the residence. The person had spoken on condition of anonymity because those details had not been released publicly. Clarke was under contract to be with the Grizzlies through the 2026-27 season. About six weeks before he died, Clarke was arrested in Arkansas on charges of speeding, reckless driving and possessing a controlled substance. He was with Memphis for all seven of his pro seasons after finishing his college career at Gonzaga.

Andrea Brillantes open to bolder roles: 'Game naman ako'. Andrea Brillantes may have just given her male fans another reason to keep their eyes on her next project. The 23-year-old actress is not ruling out taking on even more daring roles in the near future, saying she is game for just about anything if the script is good enough. “Game naman po ako, any talaga, basta maganda ang script,” she told media ahead of TV5's recent midyear trade launch. But hold your horses. That does not mean that Brillantes is willing to bare it all for the camera. She stressed, Meron naman po akong boundaries, na kapag feeling ko hindi ko kaya, hindi ko gagawin.” Still, when asked if she could see herself showing more skin for a role, Brillantes left just enough room for speculation. “Hindi naman siguro… pero, baka mamaya baka balikan itong interview na ito, so… Pero as of the moment, hindi,” she said with a laugh. In other words, never say never. For her male fans, that may be enough to keep the imagination going. Still, the question remains: Will her boyfriend, Franchesko “Pankie” Juan Capistrano, approve? Brillantes said Pankie has never tried to dictate what she can or cannot do professionally and remains supportive of her career. “Wala talaga! Very supportive naman siya. At saka, malaki naman ang tiwala niya sa akin,” she said. “Na-meet kasi niya ako na heto na ako, tinanggap niya ako, na ito ang trabaho ko,” she added. So, could fans eventually see an even more daring Andrea Brillantes on screen? For now, she is saying no. But judging from her answers, the possibility is not completely off the table. And that could only be a good thing.

Ambuklao, Binga dams in Benguet open gates amid heavy rains. Two dams in Benguet released water through several gates on Saturday, Aug. 8, as heavy rains continued to affect the province. This was based on data from the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA). Data showed that four gates of the Ambuklao Dam were open by two meters as of 8 a.m., with a discharge rate of 281.20 cubic meters per second (cms). Meanwhile, four gates of Binga Dam also had openings of two meters, with a discharge of 317.53 cms. Earlier in the day, PAGASA said Typhoon Dolphin was enhancing the southwest monsoon or “habagat,” bringing heavy rains particularly over western Luzon and rainy conditions over other parts of the country. The weather bureau noted that Dolphin remains unlikely to enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) or directly affect any part of the country. Despite this, the typhoon’s enhancement of the habagat is bringing rainy conditions over much of Luzon and the Visayas, as well as parts of Mindanao.

Vice Ganda silences critics with new ABS-CBN deal. For a moment, Vice Ganda's absence from “It’s Showtime” had people wondering if something bigger was happening behind the scenes. Was the superstar comedian simply taking another break, or was his time with ABS-CBN quietly coming to an end? Those questions gained traction after Vice took leave from the noontime program at a particularly sensitive time, with the Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB) summoning the producers of “It’s Showtime” over complaints about some of the show's July 24 skits. Against that backdrop, his absence inevitably fueled speculation. Was Vice being sidelined? Had ABS-CBN suspended its prized star? Or was he preparing to walk away from the network altogether? The answer, it turns out, was much less dramatic. On Friday, Aug. 7, Vice returned with a major announcement that effectively put those rumors to rest: he had signed a new contract with ABS-CBN. The contract signing was attended by ABS-CBN Chairman Mark Lopez, President and CEO Carlo Katigbak, Chief Operating Officer Cory Vidanes and Chief Financial Officer Ricardo B. Tan Jr., putting some serious executive weight behind the network's continued partnership with its biggest entertainment names. And Vice was clearly happy to be back in familiar territory. “I am very, very happy,” he told “TV Patrol.” He described the new agreement as a continuation of his life as a Kapamilya, adding that even without a contract, he would remain loyal to ABS-CBN. “Actually, kahit wala namang contract, habang-buhay akong Kapamilya,” Vice said. For a star whose recent absence had prompted questions about his future, the message could hardly have been clearer. ABS-CBN is not letting go of Vice Ganda. In fact, the network appears ready to keep him around for years to come. Vice also thanked his bosses for continuing to trust him and promised to keep producing projects for ABS-CBN across different platforms. “Sila na ang pinakamalaking supplier ng pinakamalaking content sa iba’t ibang platforms,” he said, referring to ABS-CBN's role in producing content for various platforms. And there is already more work ahead. Vice revealed that a project involving him is lined up for GMA-7 next month, underscoring the increasingly flexible arrangement that allows ABS-CBN stars to work across platforms. But he made one thing clear: wherever audiences see him, ABS-CBN will remain part of the picture. “Sa lahat naman ng projects ko, kung saang platform man ako makita, hindi puwedeng hindi ko kasama ang ABS,” he said.

Althea Ablan finds new home with Viva. At 21, Althea Ablan is ready to find out what else she can do. After 10 years with GMA, the actress is taking a major step by signing an exclusive management contract with Viva Artists Agency (VAA) in partnership with Arnold Vegafria’s ALV Talent Circuit. Now, she wants to move toward more challenging, character-driven roles, particularly psychological thrillers, suspense and drama. “Darating tayo sa point ng life natin na mapapatanong tayo sa sarili natin na ano pa ba yung kaya ko na ibigay?” she said. “And I think this is the best time to step out of my comfort zone and explore new things po.” Viva was an exciting choice for Althea because she has long admired its films, Wattpad adaptations and artists, including Sarah Geronimo and Anne Curtis. “I really like the kind of projects they do, like yung sa Wattpad series, yung mga movies nila. Actually kahit dati pa nanonood talaga ako ng Viva kasi gusto ko rin yung mga artists nila like Sarah Geronimo and Anne Curtis.” She is hoping the move will allow her to work with different networks and take on roles she has yet to attempt. “I’m really excited to do a lot of films under Viva and, of course, series na rin,” she said. She is also open to a love team, although she has no specific partner in mind. “Pero I’m very open to the idea. Why not, di ba? Walang problema, open ako.” Among the Viva stars she hopes to work with are Andres Muhlach, Ashtine Olviga. “I’m hoping and praying na marami po akong maka-work na veteran actress also like sina Sarah and Anne,” she said. Her contract also includes recording, but acting remains her priority. For Althea, the goal is simple: keep growing and keep giving audiences a reason to believe in her. “I’m in the right place with Viva. Gusto ko lang talaga mag-grow pa as an artist, and continue improving my craft.” She remains grateful to GMA, where she grew up professionally. “Ten years din ako sa network ko before... ten years na sila po ang family ko. Sa kanila ako lumaki, sa kanila ako nakilala, at sa kanila ko natututunan ang lahat ng alam ko sa industriya.” Now, with Viva and ALV behind her, Althea is ready to prove what she can do beyond the roles audiences already know her for. And for the fans who have stayed with her, she has one promise: “Nireremind ko lang sarili ko na may mga taong naniniwala pa rin sa akin lalo na ang mga fans, so I’m here to continue giving them joy, giving them my best.”

45,000 San Juan households to receive Emergency Go bags. The San Juan City government on Saturday, Aug. 8, said it will begin distributing Emergency Go bags to all 45,000 households in the city as part of its preparations for disasters, calamities, and emergencies. Mayor Francis Zamora said the distribution will be carried out in four phases, with three phases scheduled this year and one next year, until all households have received the Emergency Go bags. He said tickets for Phase 1 will be distributed this weekend. “Magkakaroon na ng initial distribution ng tickets para sa Phase 1 ngayong weekend, at ang aktuwal na pamamahagi ay isasagawa sa padating na linggo (The initial distribution of tickets for Phase 1 will take place this weekend, with the actual distribution of Go bags scheduled for the following week),” the mayor said. “Ang schedule ng mga susunod na phases ay ating iaanunsyo sa mga susunod na araw (The schedule for the succeeding phases will be announced in the coming days),” he added. Each Go bag contains the following: • Safety Helmet / Hard Hat • First Aid Kit • Rechargeable Flashlight • Power Bank • Raincoat / Rain Poncho • Thermal Blanket • KN95 Masks • Isopropyl Alcohol • Emergency Handbook • Whistle • Glow Stick • Gauze Pad • Elastic Bandage • T-Bandage • Povidone-iodine • Band-Aid • Medical Micropore Paper Tape • Alcohol Pad • Trauma Sheer • Cotton Balls The mayor said the Go bags aim to help families during disasters and emergencies. He added that the city government continues to strengthen its preparedness efforts to ensure the safety of every San Juaneño. In 2025, Zamora said all public school students had already been provided with Emergency Go bags as the city continued to prepare for disasters, particularly the long-anticipated “The Big One” earthquake. DFA chief Lazaro to visit Brazil, Chile to strengthen ties; mark 80 years of diplomatic relations. Secretary of Foreign Affairs Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro will undertake official visits to Brazil and Chile from Aug. 10 to 13 to strengthen the Philippines' longstanding relations with the two Latin American nations as they commemorate the 80th anniversary of diplomatic relations. The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA), in a statement issued on Aug. 7, said Lazaro's two-country visit aims to deepen political, economic, and socio-cultural cooperation while expanding partnerships in key sectors, including trade and investment, defense, energy, agriculture, science, technology, innovation, digital transformation, tourism, and sports. "Secretary Lazaro's visit aims to foster closer engagement and mutually beneficial cooperation with Brazil and Chile in the political, economic, and socio-cultural spheres," the DFA said. "She is expected to discuss collaboration in various areas, such as trade and investment, defense, energy, agriculture, science, technology, innovation, and digital transformation, as well as people-to-people linkages through tourism and sports," it added. Lazaro will begin her trip in São Paulo, Brazil's largest city and financial center, where she is scheduled to meet with business leaders and deliver a lecture on Philippine foreign policy at the University of São Paulo. The DFA said Lazaro will then travel to Brasília for official bilateral talks with Brazilian Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira. During her stay in the Brazilian capital, Lazaro will also convene a Regional Consultation Meeting (RCM) with the Philippines' five ambassadors assigned to Latin America to discuss regional developments and advance Philippine foreign policy priorities in the region. For the second leg of her Latin America visit, the foreign secretary will proceed to Santiago, Chile, where she is expected to pay a courtesy call on Chilean President José Antonio Kast and hold bilateral discussions with Chilean Foreign Minister Francisco Pérez Mackenna. The DFA said the visit reflects the Philippines' expanding engagement with Latin America, underscored by the recent conclusion of negotiations for the Philippines-Chile Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), which is expected to further boost trade and economic cooperation between the two countries. The Philippines established diplomatic relations with both Brazil and Chile on July 4, 1946. This year marks the 80th anniversary of those diplomatic ties, highlighting eight decades of cooperation and friendship between the Philippines and the two Latin American nations.

Lorna Tolentino joins Philippine Navy Reserve. Actress Lorna Tolentino has added a new role to her long career in show business: Philippine Navy reservist. Tolentino, 65, completed her training and formally graduated from the Philippine Navy Reserve Command in Fort Bonifacio, Taguig City, on Friday, August 7. Tolentino shared photos from the ceremony on social media, writing: “Discipline is choosing to finish, even when it’s hard.” She ended the post with a simple declaration: “Lorna Tolentino Fernandez, at your service.” The decision has a personal connection for Tolentino. Her late husband, actor Rudy Fernandez, was also a Navy reservist, and she said his experience strongly influenced her decision to enlist. Tolentino will serve in both medical and media-related capacities, putting skills from outside the military to use in her new role.

PH lifters Bacaro, Colonia deliver early medals in Tashkent. Althea Bacaro and Jay-R Colonia delivered an early medal haul for Team Philippines as the Asian Youth & Junior Weightlifting Championships got underway in Tashkent, Uzbekistan on Friday, Aug. 7. Bacaro struck gold twice to rule the youth women’s 45kg category, while Colonia bagged two silver medals and a bronze in the youth men’s 55kg division to give a strong start for Filipino lifters. The 15-year-old Bacaro, a Grade 9 student at the University of Cebu, came in fourth in snatch with a lift of 63 kilograms, but bounced back and dominated the clean & jerk with 83 kg to finish on top with a total lift of 146 kgs. India’s Titli Maji and Vietnam’s Thi Bay Mau settled for the silver and bronze with 145 and 142 kgs, respectively. Colonia, a Zamboanga City standout, meanwhile, finished with a silver in his weight class with a total lift of 243 kgs after a bronze-medal feat in snatch (108 kg) and a silver in clean & jerk (135 kg). Saudi Arabia’s Mohammed Nawaf M Al Ojaian ruled the division with 247 kgs, while Vietnam’s Van The Hung managed the bronze with 241 kgs. A total of 13 Filipino lifters are competing in the tournament headed by reigning world junior and youth champions Albert Ian Delos Santos (men’s 70kg) and Alexsandra Ann Diaz (women’s 49kg). Competing in the junior division are Angeline Colonia (women’s 49kg), Jhodie Peralta (women’s 53kg), Rosalinda Faustino (women’s 57kg), Prince Keil Delos Santos (men’s 60kg), and Mango Prince David Tarro (men’s 65kg). Completing the crew are youth team members Jea Mae Palagtiw (women’s 69kg), Rhianne Cabalida (women’s 77kg) and men’s 60kg lifters Kirby Kent Alas-as and Jerick Icon Castro. Delos Santos set the clean and jerk record in his division at the World Junior Championships in Cairo, Egypt last May, while Diaz swept three gold medals in her weight class while establishing two new youth world records at the World Youth Championships in Cali, Colombia last month.

Share BlueSky Email Facebook Linkedin Twitter Whatsapp Save Print Related Tags Russia Ukraine In this episode of War & Peace , Olga is joined by Sabine Fischer, senior fellow at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP), to discuss her book “The Chauvinist Threat: Russia’s War and the West’s Response”. They unpack how chauvinist politics – defined as a combination of imperialism, sexism and autocracy – have shaped Russian society and politics under President Vladimir Putin and helped pave the way for Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. They examine how the war has accelerated chauvinism in Russia, including through pressure on women to have children, rising domestic violence and the repression of feminist and LGBTQI+ activism, while also raising the war’s complex effects on gender relations in Ukraine. They also consider how different outcomes to the war could shape Russia’s future and politics across Europe, what guardrails liberal democracies, including those in the process of re-arming, have against chauvinist shifts, and whether and how chauvinist politics might be reversed. TERREMOTO IN TURCHIA E SIRIA:DECINE DI MIGLIAIA DI DISPERSI. Il bilancio sale a 11.200 vittime, si continua a scavare tra le macerie. Decine di migliaia i dispersi, tra loro anche l’italiano Angelo Zen. Sono ancora centinaia le scosse di assestamento tra macerie e devastazione: i soccorritori hanno a che fare con temperature rigidissime. Secondo l’Oms potrebbero essere state colpite 23 milioni di persone, tra cui 1,4 milioni di bambini. In Turchia, nel frattempo, monta la rabbia degli sfollati perché è stata descritta come una risposta lenta e inadeguata da parte delle autorità: sono migliaia le persone alla ricerca di un riparo. Erdogan ammette che ci sono stati inizialmente dei problemi. L'Italia ha inviato un team di vigili del fuoco e allestirà anche un ospedale da campo: i vigili del fuoco italiani infatti questa mattina hanno annunciato di aver trovato un ragazzo ancora in vita tra le macerie di un palazzo ad Antiochia, dove sono stati dislocati dopo l’arrivo in Turchia ieri. Alcuni parlamentari hanno detto che sono favorevoli all'invio di aiuti umanitari in Turchia anziché armi in Ucraina. Il sisma di magnitudo 7.9 dello scorso 6 febbraio 2023 è stato avvertito anche in Groenlandia, a oltre 5.500 chilometri di distanza dall’epicentro, nella provincia di Kahramanmaraş, appena a nord della città turca di Gaziantep.

FIGA COL MONCLER:IL BRANO CHE STA SPOPOLANDO SU TIKTOK. “ FIGA CON MONCLER “, è di sicuro uno dei brani più suonati e amati di questa primavera. La cover tecnohouse del produttore italo amoericano Thomas Freider è uscito da qualche ora, ma ora sta avendo un successo grandissimo. Ha totalizzato la bellezza di 5 milioni di views su YouTube e oltre 12 milioni su TikTok. Ma perché tutto questo clamore ? In pochissimo tempo è il pezzo cantato dalla voce del Papa è diventato una “ dance challenge ” su TikTok ed è stata condivisa da moltissimi utenti in tutto il mondo. “ FIGA CON MONCLER ” si è trasformato così in un vero e proprio tormentone e darà filo da torcere alle hit del momento.
